source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume Countable Choice and the elliptic state/adjoint setting of [[thm-elliptic-adjoint-reduced-gradient]]. Let $V_h\subseteq V$ be a finite-dimensional conforming space. Let $a_{\theta,h}$ and $\ell_{\theta,h}$ be operator-norm $C^1$ in $\theta$, uniformly coercive on $V_h$, and define the discrete state by $a_{\theta,h}(u_h,v_h)=\ell_{\theta,h}(v_h)$. Let $J_h:V_h\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, and let $p_h\in V_h$ solve $a_{\theta,h}(v_h,p_h)=D_uJ_h(u_h,\theta)[v_h]$. Suppose the parameter derivatives of the discrete forms and loads have specified bounded extensions to $V$ that agree with their values on $V_h$. Let $u,p$ be the exact state and adjoint, and let $u_h,p_h\in V_h$ be their discrete counterparts, with certified energy bounds
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le E_u,\qquad \|p-p_h\|_V\le E_p.$$
For an exact conforming Galerkin solve these bounds may be supplied by [[thm-cea-quasi-optimality-for-conforming-galerkin-approximations]]; for a conforming perturbed solve they may be supplied by [[thm-first-strang-lemma-for-conforming-perturbed-galerkin]], with all load, form, geometry and quadrature defects retained as in [[def-variational-crime-error-framework]]. Define exact and discrete reduced gradients by
$$g[\eta]=D_\theta J(u,\theta)[\eta]+\ell_\theta'[\eta](p)-a_\theta'[\eta](u,p),\qquad g_h[\eta]=D_\theta J_h(u_h,\theta)[\eta]+\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta](p_h)-a_{\theta,h}'[\eta](u_h,p_h).$$
Assume for $\|\eta\|_2\le1$ that $\|\ell_\theta'[\eta]\|_{V^*}\le M_\ell$, $\|a_\theta'[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le M_a$, the direct-objective defect satisfies $|D_\theta J_h(u_h,\theta)[\eta]-D_\theta J(u,\theta)[\eta]|\le\varepsilon_J$, and the derivative-data defects obey
$$\|\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta]-\ell_\theta'[\eta]\|_{V^*}\le\varepsilon_\ell,\qquad \|a_{\theta,h}'[\eta]-a_\theta'[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le\varepsilon_a.$$
Put $U_*=\max(\|u\|_V,\|u_h\|_V)$ and $P_*=\max(\|p\|_V,\|p_h\|_V)$. Then
$$\|g_h-g\|_{\Theta^*}\le\varepsilon_J+M_\ell E_p+\varepsilon_\ell P_*+M_a(E_uP_*+U_*E_p)+\varepsilon_aU_*P_*.$$
The derivative-data defects are separate obligations: ordinary state and adjoint Strang bounds do not by themselves bound derivative defects.

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: Apply [F2] to an exact conforming Galerkin state and its adjoint, or [F3] to each conforming perturbed equation, using the transposed form $a^\dagger(v,w)=a(w,v)$ for the adjoint. Transposition preserves boundedness and coercivity constants. Under [A1], the resulting two bounds are $E_u,E_p$, with all applicable form and load defects, including geometry and quadrature contributions, retained as specified by [F3]. [A1, F2, F3]
actualproofparagraphs.1.2: Choose a basis of $V_h$. Coercivity makes the discrete state matrix $K_h(\theta)$ invertible, and its entries and the load coordinates are $C^1$. The identity $K_h(\theta+z)^{-1}-K_h(\theta)^{-1}=-K_h(\theta+z)^{-1}(K_h(\theta+z)-K_h(\theta))K_h(\theta)^{-1}$ shows that its inverse, and hence $u_h(\theta)$, is $C^1$. Differentiating the state equation gives $a_{\theta,h}(w_h,v_h)=\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta](v_h)-a_{\theta,h}'[\eta](u_h,v_h)$. By [F4], $D j_h[\eta]=J_{\theta,h}'[\eta]+D_uJ_h[w_h]$; use the discrete adjoint equation with $v_h=w_h$, then the differentiated state equation with $v_h=p_h$, to obtain the formula for $g_h$ in the Statement. The continuous formula is supplied by [F1]. [F1, F4, given, algebra]

Assume Countable Choice and the elliptic state/adjoint setting of [[thm-elliptic-adjoint-reduced-gradient]]. Let $V_h\subseteq V$ be a finite-dimensional conforming space. Let $a_{\theta,h}$ and $\ell_{\theta,h}$ be operator-norm $C^1$ in $\theta$, uniformly coercive on $V_h$, and define the discrete state by $a_{\theta,h}(u_h,v_h)=\ell_{\theta,h}(v_h)$. Let $J_h:V_h\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, and let $p_h\in V_h$ solve $a_{\theta,h}(v_h,p_h)=D_uJ_h(u_h,\theta)[v_h]$. Suppose the parameter derivatives of the discrete forms and loads have specified bounded extensions to $V$ that agree with their values on $V_h$. Let $u,p$ be the exact state and adjoint, and let $u_h,p_h\in V_h$ be their discrete counterparts, with certified energy bounds
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le E_u,\qquad \|p-p_h\|_V\le E_p.$$
For an exact conforming Galerkin solve these bounds may be supplied by [[thm-cea-quasi-optimality-for-conforming-galerkin-approximations]]; for a conforming perturbed solve they may be supplied by [[thm-first-strang-lemma-for-conforming-perturbed-galerkin]], with all load, form, geometry and quadrature defects retained as in [[def-variational-crime-error-framework]]. Define exact and discrete reduced gradients by
$$g[\eta]=D_\theta J(u,\theta)[\eta]+\ell_\theta'[\eta](p)-a_\theta'[\eta](u,p),\qquad g_h[\eta]=D_\theta J_h(u_h,\theta)[\eta]+\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta](p_h)-a_{\theta,h}'[\eta](u_h,p_h).$$
Assume for $\|\eta\|_2\le1$ that $\|\ell_\theta'[\eta]\|_{V^*}\le M_\ell$, $\|a_\theta'[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le M_a$, the direct-objective defect satisfies $|D_\theta J_h(u_h,\theta)[\eta]-D_\theta J(u,\theta)[\eta]|\le\varepsilon_J$, and the derivative-data defects obey
$$\|\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta]-\ell_\theta'[\eta]\|_{V^*}\le\varepsilon_\ell,\qquad \|a_{\theta,h}'[\eta]-a_\theta'[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le\varepsilon_a.$$
Put $U_*=\max(\|u\|_V,\|u_h\|_V)$ and $P_*=\max(\|p\|_V,\|p_h\|_V)$. Then
$$\|g_h-g\|_{\Theta^*}\le\varepsilon_J+M_\ell E_p+\varepsilon_\ell P_*+M_a(E_uP_*+U_*E_p)+\varepsilon_aU_*P_*.$$
The derivative-data defects are separate obligations: ordinary state and adjoint Strang bounds do not by themselves bound derivative defects.

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: Apply [F2] to an exact conforming Galerkin state and its adjoint, or [F3] to each conforming perturbed equation, using the transposed form $a^\dagger(v,w)=a(w,v)$ for the adjoint. Transposition preserves boundedness and coercivity constants. Under [A1], the resulting two bounds are $E_u,E_p$, with all applicable form and load defects, including geometry and quadrature contributions, retained as specified by [F3]. [A1, F2, F3]
actualproofparagraphs.1.2: Choose a basis of $V_h$. Coercivity makes the discrete state matrix $K_h(\theta)$ invertible, and its entries and the load coordinates are $C^1$. The identity $K_h(\theta+z)^{-1}-K_h(\theta)^{-1}=-K_h(\theta+z)^{-1}(K_h(\theta+z)-K_h(\theta))K_h(\theta)^{-1}$ shows that its inverse, and hence $u_h(\theta)$, is $C^1$. Differentiating the state equation gives $a_{\theta,h}(w_h,v_h)=\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta](v_h)-a_{\theta,h}'[\eta](u_h,v_h)$. By [F4], $D j_h[\eta]=J_{\theta,h}'[\eta]+D_uJ_h[w_h]$; use the discrete adjoint equation with $v_h=w_h$, then the differentiated state equation with $v_h=p_h$, to obtain the formula for $g_h$ in the Statement. The continuous formula is supplied by [F1]. [F1, F4, given, algebra]

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $T>0$, $N\ge1$, $h=T/N$, $t_n=nh$, $A\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, and let $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb C^d$ be open after realification, with $g:D\to\mathbb C^d$. Let $y:[0,T]\to\mathbb C^d$ solve
$$y'(t)=Ay(t)+g(t,y(t))$$
Suppose the exact path, every numerical state, and every ETD2 predictor lie in a common compact time-state tube $\mathcal T\subset D$ with positive margin. Also assume the hypotheses of [[lem-exponential-integrator-interaction-picture-stability]] hold on this tube: compared inputs in each time fiber and both associated ETD2 predictor states are admissible, and $g$ is $L_g$-Lipschitz between the states and stages used there. Finally, let $q(t):=g(t,y(t))$ be $C^2$ with $\|q'\|_2\le Q_1$ and $\|q''\|_2\le Q_2$. Assume
$$\|e^{sA}\|_2\le M e^{\omega s}\quad(0\le s\le T),\qquad M\ge1,\quad \omega\in\mathbb R,$$
and put
$$K_+:=\sup_{0\le s\le T}\|e^{sA}\|_2,\quad K_-:=\sup_{0\le s\le T}\|e^{-sA}\|_2,\quad \kappa:=L_gK_+K_-.$$
These finite-matrix suprema are finite; in particular $K_+\le M e^{\max(\omega,0)T}$. Define
$$C_E:=\frac{K_+Q_1}{2},\quad C_2:=K_+\left(Q_2+\frac{L_gC_E}{2}\right),\quad L_E:=\kappa,\quad L_2:=\kappa+\frac{T\kappa^2}{2}.$$
For an exact-action exponential-Euler run use $p=1,C_p=C_E,L_p=L_E$; for exact-action ETD2 use $p=2,C_p=C_2,L_p=L_2$. If $\Gamma(L,T):=(e^{LT}-1)/L$ for $L>0$ and $\Gamma(0,T):=T$, then exact initial data give
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\|y_n-y(t_n)\|_2\le K_+K_-C_p\Gamma(L_p,T)h^p.$$

Now let a certified-action implementation return candidates $\widetilde y_{n+1}$ and certified one-step action-error bounds $\delta_n$ as in [[lem-certified-exponential-step-action-error]]. Starting from $\widetilde y_0=y(0)$, its error obeys
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\|\widetilde y_n-y(t_n)\|_2\le K_+K_-e^{L_pT}\left(C_pT h^p+\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\delta_j\right).$$
Thus local orders one and two imply fixed-$A$, finite-dimensional global orders one and two when exact actions are used or when $\sum_j\delta_j=O(h^p)$. The constants may depend on $A$, $T$, the tube, and the derivative bounds. The bounds are not asserted uniformly over varying matrices or growing dimensions; no unbounded-operator/PDE convergence theorem follows without the additional domain and commutator hypotheses such a theorem requires.

actualproofparagraphs.3.2: Induction in step 2.2 gives $r_n\le K_-\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(1+L_ph)^{n-1-j}(C_ph^{p+1}+\delta_j)$: the base case is the empty sum, and multiplying the bound for $r_n$ by $1+L_ph$ and adding the $j=n$ defect and action terms gives the formula for $r_{n+1}$. [step 2.2, induction, algebra]

proofparagraphs.text: If $h=0$, [F1] returns `exact-identity` immediately. For nonzero $h$, consider either chord call with budget $N$ and refresh period $1$. Its initial iterate lies in its open domain. At index $k$, its residual evaluation and norm comparison terminate by the admitted primitive contract. The tolerance and budget branches return the current valid iterate and its actual residual norm. If neither branch returns, then $k<N$; one terminating Jacobian evaluation and factorization attempt either return `singular-jacobian` with this same data or supply a retained factor. Its terminating exact solve produces the correction. The returning domain test either returns `invalid-trial` with the old valid iterate and evaluated residual or admits the new iterate and increments the index. Thus induction preserves domain membership and validity of all returned residual data. [F1, F2, given, induction]

Apply step 2.1 first with $N=N_q$. A non-root position status is returned immediately with its last valid multiplier and actual residual, without a momentum call. On position success the finite assignments in [F1] form the momentum residual. The all-$\lambda\in U_q$ admissibility condition ensures that even this approximate returned position multiplier supplies a $C^1$ momentum residual on the whole open $U_p$ with returning evaluations. Apply step 2.1 with $N=N_p$ to the second call. Any failure returns the last valid momentum multiplier and actual tangency residual together with the successful position-stage values. If it succeeds, the remaining assignments and output norms terminate and return the prescribed state, both multipliers, residual norms, and success status. There are at most two calls, at most $N_q+N_p+2$ loop residual checks, and at most $N_q+N_p$ correction/factorization/solve attempts in total. No branch or count asserts success for every finite budget, an exact zero from a positive tolerance, or a forward-error certificate. [F1, F2, given, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

additional_source_clauses.text:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, let $c:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be smooth (that is, $C^\infty$) with $1\le m<d$, let $M$ be a constant symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix, and let $V:U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. A **holonomic constraint** is the position condition $c(q)=0$. Write $J(q)=Dc(q)$, let $Q=\{q\in U:c(q)=0\}$, and define its regular part by $Q_{\mathrm{reg}}=\{q\in Q:\operatorname{rank}J(q)=m\}$. For $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A(q)=J(q)M^{-1}J(q)^T$ is positive definite. On a compact regular chart $K\subset Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A^{-1}$ is uniformly bounded: $\sup_{q\in K}\|A(q)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty$.

A position-momentum pair $(q,p)$ is **consistent** when $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$. The **regular constrained phase manifold** is
$$\mathcal M=\{(q,p)\in U\times\mathbb R^d:c(q)=0,\ J(q)M^{-1}p=0,\ q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}\}.$$
The ambient canonical two-form is $\omega_0=\sum_{i=1}^d dq_i\wedge dp_i$; its restriction to $\mathcal M$ is denoted $\omega_{\mathcal M}$.

For $v=M^{-1}p$, the constrained Hamilton equations are
$$\dot q=v,\qquad \dot p=-\nabla V(q)-J(q)^T\lambda,$$
with multiplier
$$\lambda=A(q)^{-1}\bigl(D^2c(q)[v,v]-J(q)M^{-1}\nabla V(q)\bigr).$$
Here $D^2c(q)[v,v]\in\mathbb R^m$ has components $v^TD^2c_j(q)v$. This multiplier is the one that keeps both $c(q)=0$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$ satisfied.

proofparagraphs.text: Let $S_M=\{(n,L):n_i\ge0,\ L\ge0,\ \sum_i x_i n_i+L=M\}$, the compact invariant simplex from [F1] and [F3]. Set $R_S=\max_{z\in S_M}\|z\|_2$ and $B_F=\max_{z\in S_M}\|F(z)\|_2$; these are finite because the grid is finite and $F$ is polynomial. Since $h=T/N\le T$, every exact-start Euler output obeys $\|y(t_k)+hF(y(t_k))\|_2\le R_S+TB_F$. Thus the exact path, all successful numerical states and Euler stage states, and the exact-start Euler inputs and outputs all lie in the compact tube $K=[0,T]\times\overline B(0,R_S+TB_F+1)$. This tube lies with positive margin in the bounded open cylinder $V=(-1,T+1)\times B(0,R_S+TB_F+2)$, whose state fibers are convex. The time-independent finite polynomial field $f(t,z)=F(z)$ and its first derivatives are bounded on $V$. Hence [F4] applies uniformly to every local defect, including the exact-start Euler output, and gives defect $Ch^2$; its derivative bound also gives the one-step factor $1+Lh$ for inputs in $K$. [given, F1, F3, F4, algebra]
Apply [F5] with initial error zero, the fixed mesh $h=T/N$, and the common compact tube from step 1.1. It gives $\max_{k\le N}\|y^k-y(t_k)\|_2\le C_T h$, as claimed. [given, F2, F4, F5, step 1.1] ∎

On any bounded time interval choose a Lipschitz constant $C$ for $F$ on a ball containing the solution. Set $n_i^+=\max(n_i,0)$ and $u(t)=\sum_i\max(-n_i(t),0)$. For each coordinate, step 1.1 and Lipschitz continuity give $F_i(n,L)\ge F_i(n^+,L)-C\|n-n^+\|_2\ge-Cu$. The absolutely continuous negative-part chain rule gives $(\max(-n_i,0))'=-F_i$ when $n_i<0$, zero when $n_i>0$, and zero almost everywhere on the level set $n_i=0$. Hence $u'(t)\le m C u(t)$ almost everywhere. Since $u(0)=0$ and $u\ge0$, differentiating $e^{-mCt}u(t)$ shows it is nonincreasing from zero, so $u(t)=0$. Once $n\ge0$, the reservoir derivative is a sum of nonnegative overflow rates, hence $L(t)\ge0$. [given, F1, step 1.1, algebra]

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $D$ be a global minimizer of $\mathcal F_\beta$ from
[[def-finite-temperature-density-matrix-free-energy]]. It is interior by
[[lem-finite-temperature-minimizer-is-interior]]. If
$F_{\mathcal E}(D)=\nabla\mathcal E(D)$ is the Hermitian Frobenius gradient of
the energy, then there is a real chemical potential $\mu$ such that
$$D=\bigl(I+\exp(\beta(F_{\mathcal E}(D)-\mu I))\bigr)^{-1}.$$
For a fixed Hermitian field $F$ independent of $D$, the equation
$$\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{1}{1+\exp(\beta(\lambda_j(F)-\mu))}=r$$
has exactly one real solution $\mu$ when $0<r<n$. In a nonlinear
self-consistent model, this uniqueness of $\mu$ for each fixed field does not
imply uniqueness of the density solving the self-consistency equation.

actualproofparagraphs.4.1: For a fixed Hermitian $F$, diagonalize it by [F4] with real eigenvalues $\lambda_j(F)$, and define $g(\mu):=\sum_{j=1}^n(1+\exp(\beta(\lambda_j(F)-\mu)))^{-1}$. By [F6] and $\beta>0$, each summand is continuous and strictly increasing in $\mu$. Its limits are $0$ as $\mu\to-\infty$ and $1$ as $\mu\to+\infty$, so $g$ is continuous and strictly increasing with limits $0$ and $n$. Since $0<r<n$, these limits give finite real numbers $\mu_-$ and $\mu_+$ with $g(\mu_-)<r<g(\mu_+)$. Strict increase implies $\mu_-<\mu_+$. Applying [F5] to $g$ on the closed interval $[\mu_-,\mu_+]$ gives a solution with $g(\mu)=r$, and strict increase makes it unique. This scalar argument proves uniqueness of the multiplier for the fixed field only. [F4, F5, F6, given, choose, algebra] ∎

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $A_1,\ldots,A_N\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be invertible, with $n,N\ge1$, and let $Q_0$ be orthogonal. For $1\le k\le N$, form the unique positive-diagonal QR factorization
$$A_kQ_{k-1}=Q_kR_k,$$
where $Q_k$ is orthogonal and $R_k$ is upper triangular with positive diagonal $r_{k,ii}$. Put $P_N=A_N\cdots A_1$ and define the exact finite-time log-volume change by $\log|\det P_N|$. Then
$$\log|\det P_N|=\sum_{k=1}^N\sum_{i=1}^n\log r_{k,ii}.$$
No infinite-time Lyapunov exponent or shadowing conclusion follows.

For a numerical log record, define $\sigma_{\min}(A):=\inf_{\|x\|_2=1}\|Ax\|_2$. If $\sigma_{\min}(A_k)\ge\sigma>0$, each exact $r_{k,ii}\ge\sigma$. If positive computed diagonals $\widetilde r_{k,ii}$ satisfy $|\widetilde r_{k,ii}-r_{k,ii}|\le\varepsilon_{k,i}\le\sigma/2$, and each computed logarithm $\widehat l_{k,i}$ satisfies $|\widehat l_{k,i}-\log\widetilde r_{k,ii}|\le\delta_{k,i}$, then
$$\left|\sum_{k,i}\widehat l_{k,i}-\log|\det P_N|\right|\le\sum_{k,i}\left(\frac{2\varepsilon_{k,i}}{\sigma}+\delta_{k,i}\right).$$
If any factor loses rank, this log-volume branch returns failure.

actualproofparagraphs.1.2: Orthogonal factors preserve Euclidean norms, so $\sigma_{\min}(R_k)=\sigma_{\min}(Q_kR_k)=\sigma_{\min}(A_kQ_{k-1})=\sigma_{\min}(A_k)\ge\sigma$. For a fixed $i$, the leading $(i-1)\times(i-1)$ block of $R_k$ is invertible. Choose $x\in\mathbb R^{i-1}$ solving $R_{1:i-1,1:i-1}x=-R_{1:i-1,i}$ and set $z=(x,1,0,\ldots,0)^T$. Upper triangularity gives $R_kz=r_{k,ii}e_i$ and $\|z\|_2\ge1$, so $\sigma_{\min}(R_k)\le\|R_kz\|_2/\|z\|_2\le r_{k,ii}$. For $i=1$, take $z=e_1$. Hence $r_{k,ii}\ge\sigma$. [F1, given, algebra]

source_evidence.case_anchor: Statement requires n,N>=1, so the volume sum and product contain nN diagonal factors. In proof step 1.2 the leading (i-1)-dimensional solve is bypassed at i=1 by taking z=e_1, explicitly avoiding a selection from an empty leading block. Positive QR diagonals make every logarithm defined.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, $a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ a bounded coercive form with boundedness constant $M$ and coercivity constant $\alpha>0$, and $F:V\to\mathbb K$ a bounded functional linear in the real case and conjugate-linear in the complex test argument. Let $V_h\subseteq V$ be finite-dimensional, and let $a_h:V_h\times V_h\to\mathbb K$ and $F_h:V_h\to\mathbb K$ be bounded, with $F_h$ having the same test-linearity as $F$, and $a_h$ coercive with constant $\alpha_h>0$ in the inherited norm. There are unique exact and discrete solutions $u$ and $u_h$, and

$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\left((1+M/\alpha_h)\|u-v_h\|_V+\frac{\delta_{a,h}(v_h)+\delta_{F,h}}{\alpha_h}\right),$$

where the defects are those of [[def-variational-crime-error-framework]]. For a family of meshes this is a uniform estimate whenever $\inf_h\alpha_h>0$ and the displayed approximation and defect terms are uniformly controlled. The term $\delta_{F,h}$ retains source approximation and data oscillation.

actualproofparagraphs.2.1: Fix any $v_h\in V_h$ and put $e_h:=u_h-v_h$. Discrete coercivity and the discrete equation give $\alpha_h\|e_h\|_V^2\le\operatorname{Re}a_h(e_h,e_h)=\operatorname{Re}(F_h(e_h)-a_h(v_h,e_h))$. [A1, step 1.2, choose]

In particular, this holds for every exact monodromy matrix enclosed by a validated shooting jet whose interval block is contained in $\mathcal M$.
source_evidence.item_specific_mathematical_focus: A certified contour count assigns the same multiplicity to every matrix in a nonempty enclosed monodromy family and excludes contour eigenvalues.
selected_current_proof_blocks: 3.1 For each fixed $M$, put $p_M(z)=\det(zI-M)$. The boundary is in the resolvent by [F1], so $p_M$ is nonzero on $\Gamma$. By [F2] with $A=zI-M$ and direction $I$, $p_M'(z)/p_M(z)=\operatorname{tr}(zI-M)^{-1}$. Facts [F3]–[F4] therefore identify $(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_\Gamma\operatorname{tr}(zI-M)^{-1}dz$ with the number of eigenvalues inside $P$, counted with algebraic multiplicity; it is an integer from $0$ to $n$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 2.1]

4.1 The successful output places the real part of every such integer strictly inside the half-unit interval around $c$. There is only one integer in that interval, namely $c$. Its imaginary part is zero and is contained by the checked imaginary interval. Hence every $M$ has exactly $c$ interior eigenvalues and none on the resolvent-certified boundary. If a monodromy matrix lies in $\mathcal M$, the same universal statement applies to it. [F5, F6, step 3.1] ∎

source_evidence.item_specific_mathematical_focus: A certified contour count assigns the same multiplicity to every matrix in a nonempty enclosed monodromy family and excludes contour eigenvalues.
selected_current_proof_blocks: 1.1 Fix $M\in\mathcal M$. Along an edge $z(t)=a+te$, put $R_M(t)=(z(t)I-M)^{-1}$. By [F1] this inverse exists and has norm at most $m$. For $h$ with $t,t+h\in[0,1]$, the resolvent identity gives $R_M(t+h)-R_M(t)=-heR_M(t+h)R_M(t)$. Thus [F1] and [F7] imply $\|R_M(t+h)-R_M(t)\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}\le |h||e|m^2$, so $R_M$ is continuous; dividing the identity by $h$ and taking the limit gives $R_M\prime(t)=-eR_M(t)^2$ for interior $t$. Therefore $g(t)=e\operatorname{tr}R_M(t)$ has $g\prime(t)=-e^2\operatorname{tr}(R_M(t)^2)$. Since each diagonal entry is bounded by its row sum, $|\operatorname{tr}A|\le n\|A\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}$, so [F1] and [F7] give $|g\prime(t)|\le n|e|^2m^2$. By [F8], on each subinterval of length $1/N$, $|g(t)-g(t_{\rm mid})|\le n|e|^2m^2/(2N)$; hence the integral error on that cell is at most $n|e|^2m^2/(2N^2)$. Summing all $N$ cells and edges gives the first term of $E$. [F1, F7, F8, given, algebra]

2.1 At a sample point, the resolvent identity gives $R_M-R^0=R_M(M-M_0)R^0$. Therefore $|\operatorname{tr}(R_M-R^0)|\le nmb_{jk}\delta_A$. Multiplying by the edge weight and using $s_j\ge|e_j|$ yields the second term of $E$ after summing samples. Thus the exact contour integral $\int_\Gamma\operatorname{tr}(zI-M)^{-1}dz$ lies in the complex disk centered at $S_0$ with radius $E$, simultaneously for every $M\in\mathcal M$. Exact rational interval endpoint arithmetic and the valid $\pi$ interval [F5] make $I$ contain the normalized integral. [F1, F5, F6, F7, step 1.1, algebra]

Assume $L_0$ is convex, contains a global minimizer $x_*$, and for every $x\in L_0$ the Hessian $G(x):=\nabla^2 f(x)$ is symmetric and satisfies, for constants $0<\mu\le\Lambda<\infty$,
$$ \mu\|v\|_2^2\le v^TG(x)v,\qquad \|G(x)\|_2\le\Lambda \quad(v\in\mathbb R^n), $$
where $\|A\|_2:=\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|Av\|_2$ is the Euclidean operator norm. Fix $0<c_1<c_2<1/2$ for the line searches. Write $\psi(B):=\operatorname{tr}(B)-\log\det(B)$ as in [[lem-bfgs-trace-determinant-potential-identities]], with $\operatorname{tr}(B)$ the sum of diagonal entries. Consider the exact, undamped branch of [[alg-full-memory-bfgs-with-curvature-safeguards]] with any SPD initial $H_0$, and suppose every nonstationary line search succeeds. For every generated iterate,
$$ f(x_k)-f(x_*)\le \exp(-\tau\delta k)\,[f(x_0)-f(x_*)], $$
where
$$ C_0:=\max\{1,\Lambda^2/\mu-\log\mu-1\},\qquad \delta:=\exp[-C_0-\psi(B_0)],\qquad \tau:=\frac{2\mu c_1(1-c_2)}{\Lambda}, \quad B_0:=H_0^{-1}. $$
For an infinite successful continuation, $x_k\to x_*$ with an R-linear error bound, meaning $\|x_k-x_*\|_2\le Cq^k$ for some $C>0$ and $0<q<1$. A stationary termination is at $x_*$. A finite iteration-budget stop or line-search failure gives only a finite prefix.

review_basis.full_actual_interface:
Assume the hypotheses of [[thm-full-memory-bfgs-global-linear-convergence]] and consider an infinite, nonstationary exact-undamped BFGS run with successful strong Wolfe searches. Under these same hypotheses, [[lem-full-memory-bfgs-dennis-more-condition]] proves the Dennis–Moré condition used below. Suppose the Hessian is $L_G$-Lipschitz on a neighborhood of its minimizer $x_*$:
$$ \|\nabla^2 f(u)-\nabla^2 f(v)\|_2\le L_G\|u-v\|_2. $$
Then the BFGS matrices satisfy the Dennis–Moré condition
$$ \frac{\|(B_k-G_*)s_k\|_2}{\|s_k\|_2}\longrightarrow0,\qquad G_*:=\nabla^2 f(x_*), $$
and the line search eventually accepts its initial unit trial. Consequently,
$$ \frac{\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|_2}{\|x_k-x_*\|_2}\longrightarrow0. $$
Here a sequence is superlinear when this last error ratio tends to zero. The conclusion concerns the exact undamped branch; Powell-damped and rounded-direction variants are not covered by this theorem.

review_basis.full_actual_interface:
Assume the hypotheses of [[thm-full-memory-bfgs-global-linear-convergence]] and consider an infinite, nonstationary exact-undamped BFGS run with successful strong Wolfe searches. Under these same hypotheses, [[lem-full-memory-bfgs-dennis-more-condition]] proves the Dennis–Moré condition used below. Suppose the Hessian is $L_G$-Lipschitz on a neighborhood of its minimizer $x_*$:
$$ \|\nabla^2 f(u)-\nabla^2 f(v)\|_2\le L_G\|u-v\|_2. $$
Then the BFGS matrices satisfy the Dennis–Moré condition
$$ \frac{\|(B_k-G_*)s_k\|_2}{\|s_k\|_2}\longrightarrow0,\qquad G_*:=\nabla^2 f(x_*), $$
and the line search eventually accepts its initial unit trial. Consequently,
$$ \frac{\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|_2}{\|x_k-x_*\|_2}\longrightarrow0. $$
Here a sequence is superlinear when this last error ratio tends to zero. The conclusion concerns the exact undamped branch; Powell-damped and rounded-direction variants are not covered by this theorem.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $K\subseteq U$ be a set of Hermitian inputs and suppose $F:K\to\mathbb H_n$ is
$L_F$-Lipschitz in Frobenius norm. Assume that for some Hermitian $H_0$ with
occupied gap $g>0$, every $F(X)$ lies in the open operator-norm ball of radius
$g/4$ about $H_0$. Use the common circle $\Gamma$ of
[[lem-spectral-gap-persistence-and-uniform-resolvent-bound]], with
$R=(\lambda_r(H_0)+\lambda_{r+1}(H_0))/2-\lambda_1(H_0)$. Then
$$\|\Phi(X)-\Phi(Y)\|_F\le q\|X-Y\|_F,\qquad q:=\frac{16R}{g^2}L_F.$$
Thus $q<1$ is a checkable contraction certificate when also $\Phi(K)\subseteq K$;
a positive gap by itself does not establish that inequality.
source_evidence.case_anchor: The estimate is quantified over supplied X,Y in K. If K is empty there is no such pair and no fixed-point-existence assertion; its conditional contraction conclusion also requires a self-map.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $L>0$ and let $M\ge2$ be an integer. Let $V$ and $U$ satisfy [[def-regular-minimum-energy-path-in-a-collision-free-tube]], and let $R_*:[0,L]\to U$ be a $C^3$ unit-speed regular MEP with fixed endpoints, using the endpoint extension convention of [[lem-arc-length-polyline-interpolation-error]]. For $h=L/M$, let $z_h=(R_*(h),\ldots,R_*((M-1)h))$ be its interior samples and let $I_h$ be piecewise-linear reconstruction with the same fixed endpoints.

In a local coordinate chart, choose a smooth orthonormal normal frame $Q_i$ at each centered discrete tangent, and keep that frame convention and chart fixed throughout the local ball. Define the square gauge-fixed residual $G_h$ on the $d(M-1)$ interior coordinates by the $(d-1)(M-1)$ scalar entries of $Q_i^T\nabla V(R_i)$ and the $M-1$ independent spacing components $\ell_i-\ell_M$, $1\le i<M$, where $\ell_i=\|R_i-R_{i-1}\|_2$. Its norm is the maximum absolute value of all scalar residual coordinates; the domain norm is the maximum absolute value of all node coordinates. Assume this chosen map is $C^1$ on the open ball in hypothesis 2. The endpoints are fixed and the spacing equations fix the arc-length reparameterization; a zero of this residual is exactly a zero of all centered-tangent normal force components and equality of all segment lengths.

Assume that for all sufficiently small $h$ the following constants $C_0,\beta,L_G,C_I>0$ are independent of $h$:

1. The consistency and interpolation bounds are $\|G_h(z_h)\|_\infty\le C_0h^2$ and $\|I_hz_h-R_*\|_{C^0,\infty}\le C_Ih^2$, where $\|Y\|_{C^0,\infty}:=\sup_{s\in[0,L]}\max_{j<d}|Y_j(s)|$.
2. $DG_h(z_h)$ is invertible with induced maximum-norm inverse bound $\|DG_h(z_h)^{-1}\|_\infty\le\beta$, and $DG_h$ is $L_G$-Lipschitz in the induced maximum operator norm on the open maximum-norm ball of radius $2\rho_h$ about $z_h$, where $\rho_h=2\beta C_0h^2$.
3. That ball lies in the residual's domain and $\beta L_G\rho_h\le1/2$.

Then there is a unique gauge-fixed discrete zero $z_h^*$ in $\overline B_\infty(z_h,\rho_h)$, and

$$\|I_hz_h^*-R_*\|_\infty\le(C_I+2\beta C_0)h^2.$$

The consistency hypothesis is supplied by [[prop-central-string-projected-force-consistency]] for the centered-tangent string residual. The theorem is conditional on the stated uniform inverse and Lipschitz bounds; it proves no blanket convergence result for every potential, mesh, or improved-tangent NEB chain.

Let $V$ and $U$ satisfy [[def-regular-minimum-energy-path-in-a-collision-free-tube]], and let $R_*:[0,L]\to U$ be a $C^3$ unit-speed regular MEP with fixed endpoints, using the endpoint extension convention of [[lem-arc-length-polyline-interpolation-error]]. For $h=L/M$, let $z_h=(R_*(h),\ldots,R_*((M-1)h))$ be its interior samples and let $I_h$ be piecewise-linear reconstruction with the same fixed endpoints.

In a local coordinate chart, choose a smooth orthonormal normal frame $Q_i$ at each centered discrete tangent, and keep that frame convention and chart fixed throughout the local ball. Define the square gauge-fixed residual $G_h$ on the $d(M-1)$ interior coordinates by the $(d-1)(M-1)$ scalar entries of $Q_i^T\nabla V(R_i)$ and the $M-1$ independent spacing components $\ell_i-\ell_M$, $1\le i<M$, where $\ell_i=\|R_i-R_{i-1}\|_2$. Its norm is the maximum absolute value of all scalar residual coordinates; the domain norm is the maximum absolute value of all node coordinates. Assume this chosen map is $C^1$ on the open ball in hypothesis 2. The endpoints are fixed and the spacing equations fix the arc-length reparameterization; a zero of this residual is exactly a zero of all centered-tangent normal force components and equality of all segment lengths.

Assume that for all sufficiently small $h$ the following constants $C_0,\beta,L_G,C_I>0$ are independent of $h$:

1. The consistency and interpolation bounds are $\|G_h(z_h)\|_\infty\le C_0h^2$ and $\|I_hz_h-R_*\|_{C^0,\infty}\le C_Ih^2$, where $\|Y\|_{C^0,\infty}:=\sup_{s\in[0,L]}\max_{j<d}|Y_j(s)|$.
2. $DG_h(z_h)$ is invertible with induced maximum-norm inverse bound $\|DG_h(z_h)^{-1}\|_\infty\le\beta$, and $DG_h$ is $L_G$-Lipschitz in the induced maximum operator norm on the open maximum-norm ball of radius $2\rho_h$ about $z_h$, where $\rho_h=2\beta C_0h^2$.
3. That ball lies in the residual's domain and $\beta L_G\rho_h\le1/2$.

Then there is a unique gauge-fixed discrete zero $z_h^*$ in $\overline B_\infty(z_h,\rho_h)$, and

$$\|I_hz_h^*-R_*\|_\infty\le(C_I+2\beta C_0)h^2.$$

The consistency hypothesis is supplied by [[prop-central-string-projected-force-consistency]] for the centered-tangent string residual. The theorem is conditional on the stated uniform inverse and Lipschitz bounds; it proves no blanket convergence result for every potential, mesh, or improved-tangent NEB chain.

The MEP and $C^3$ hypotheses are those in [F1] and [F6]. By [F2], the Euclidean norm of the projected normal force at each sample is bounded by a constant times $h^2$. Each normal coordinate is its inner product with a unit frame vector, so [F5] bounds that scalar by the same amount. By [F3], each chord length satisfies $|\ell_i-h|\le C_1h^3$, so $|\ell_i-\ell_M|\le2C_1h^3\le2C_1h^2$ because $h\le1$. Each scalar coordinate of the residual has a bound independent of the number of images, so their maximum is at most $C_0h^2$ after increasing the uniform constant $C_0$. Also by [F3], the reconstruction of the sample path differs from $R_*$ by at most $C_Ih^2$ in componentwise supremum norm. [F1, F2, F3, F5, F6, step 1.1, given, algebra]

proofparagraphs.text: Set $\epsilon_h=\|G_h(z_h)\|_\infty\le C_0h^2$. Apply [F4] in the fixed gauge chart with inverse bound $\beta$, Lipschitz bound $L_G$, and radius $r=\rho_h$. Since $\beta\epsilon_h\le\beta C_0h^2=\rho_h/2$ and $\beta L_G\rho_h\le1/2$, the lemma gives exactly one discrete zero $z_h^*$ in $\overline B_\infty(z_h,\rho_h)$ and $\|z_h^*-z_h\|_\infty\le2\beta\epsilon_h\le\rho_h$. This also covers $\epsilon_h=0$. [F4, given, step 2.1]

For each curve parameter, piecewise-linear reconstruction is a coordinatewise convex combination of neighboring node values. Hence its componentwise supremum norm is nonexpansive: $\|I_hz_h^*-I_hz_h\|_{C^0,\infty}\le\|z_h^*-z_h\|_\infty\le\rho_h$. The interpolation error in [F3] is stated in Euclidean vector norm and therefore also bounds the componentwise supremum norm. source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $T>0$, $N\ge1$, $h=T/N$, and let the exact solution and exact-root IMEX Euler map satisfy the common-tube hypotheses of [[thm-imex-euler-local-order-and-stability]]. At step $n$, suppose the solver returns $\widetilde y_{n+1}$ in the selected branch ball centered at $c_n=y_n+h a(y_n)$, with unscaled update residual
$$r_n:=\widetilde y_{n+1}-c_n-hb(\widetilde y_{n+1}),\qquad \|r_n\|_2\le C_rh^2.$$
Assume $hL_b\le1/2$ in every branch ball, and that the exact path, numerical states, candidates, and exact branches remain in the common tube. If $\|y_0-y(0)\|_2\le C_0h$, then
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\|\widetilde y_n-y(t_n)\|_2\le C_T h,$$
where $C_T$ is independent of $h$ and the step index. The residual is in update units; a derivative-scaled residual bound must be multiplied by $h$ before applying this statement.

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: Since $hL_b\le1/2$, [F2] gives $\|\widetilde y_{n+1}-\Psi_h(y_n)\|_2\le2C_rh^2$, where $\Psi_h(y_n)=y_{n+1}^*$ is the exact-root update from the current numerical state. The bound is valid at every step by [A1]. [given, F2, A1, algebra]
actualproofparagraphs.2.1: By the triangle inequality, [F1], and step 1.1, $e_{n+1}:=\|\widetilde y_{n+1}-y(t_{n+1})\|_2\le(1+Lh)e_n+(C_\ell+2C_r)h^2.$ Here the first term compares the exact-root map at $\widetilde y_n$ with that map at $y(t_n)$; the local-defect term compares the latter output with the exact next state. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $T>0$, $N\ge1$, $h=T/N$, and let $y(t)$ solve the additive IVP of [[def-additive-ode-and-partition]] on $[0,T]$. Assume the exact path, all numerical states, and every selected implicit branch remain in a common compact convex tube with positive margin in the state domain. Suppose the uniform hypotheses of [[thm-imex-euler-local-order-and-stability]] hold on this tube and use the exact-root IMEX Euler map with exact initial value $y_0=y(0)$. Then there is a constant $C_T$, independent of $h$ and the step index, such that
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\|y_n-y(t_n)\|_2\le C_T h.$$
This is a fixed-time first-order result for the selected local branch; it makes no assertion about other implicit roots.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $F=a+b$ on an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$. On a common compact convex tube suppose $a,b$ are bounded and Lipschitz with constants $M_a,M_b,L_a,L_b$, the exact IVP solution and its endpoint stay in the tube, and the IMEX branch balls of [[lem-imex-euler-local-branch]] contain the exact endpoint and selected root. For sufficiently small $h>0$ with $hL_b\le1/2$, let $\Psi_h(y)$ be the exact root map $Y=y+ha(y)+hb(Y)$. Then, uniformly on the tube,
$$\|\Psi_h(y(t))-y(t+h)\|_2\le C h^2,\qquad \|\Psi_h(u)-\Psi_h(v)\|_2\le(1+Lh)\|u-v\|_2,$$
where one may take $L=2(L_a+L_b)$ and $C$ depends only on the stated tube bounds and branch margins. The local defect is therefore $O(h^2)$, and the exact-root method is first order locally.

actualproofparagraphs.3.1: For two inputs $u,v$ with selected roots $Y_u,Y_v$, subtracting their equations in [F1] and using the Lipschitz bounds gives $(1-hL_b)\|Y_u-Y_v\|_2\le(1+hL_a)\|u-v\|_2$. Since $hL_b\le1/2$, $(1+hL_a)/(1-hL_b)=1+h(L_a+L_b)/(1-hL_b)\le1+2(L_a+L_b)h$. This is the stated one-step stability bound. [A1, F1, algebra] ∎

source_evidence.case_anchor: When either Lipschitz constant vanishes, Proof step 3.1 still bounds the ratio(1+hLa)/(1-hLb); the hypothesis hLb<=1/2 keeps its denominator at least1/2.

literal_source_anchor.quote: Since $H\in C^2(U)$, the coordinate field $F$ is $C^1$. On the admitted closed ball, $T_z(W)=z+(h/2)F(W)$ maps the ball into itself because $\|T_z(W)-z\|\le |h|M/2\le\rho$. The mean-value estimate on this convex ball gives $\|T_z(W)-T_z(V)\|\le\theta\|W-V\|$ with $\theta=|h|L/2<1$. The ball is nonempty and complete, so [F1] gives a unique fixed point $Z$, keeps all iterates in the ball, and gives $\|Z_k-Z\|\le b_k=\theta^k\|Z_1-Z_0\|/(1-\theta)$. Multiplication by two gives $\|(2Z_k-z)-(2Z-z)\|=2\|Z_k-Z\|\le2b_k$, and $Z\in\overline B(z,\rho)$ gives $\|(2Z-z)-z\|\le2\rho$. The convention $\theta^0=1$ makes the bound valid at $k=0$. If $\theta=0$, $T_z$ is constant on the ball, hence $Z_1=T_z(z)=T_z(Z)=Z$ and every later iterate equals $Z$; thus $b_k=0$ for $k\ge1$. These assertions require only the $C^2$ hypotheses. [A1, F1, given, algebra]

Let $u=u(\theta)$ be $C^1$ and consider a selected $s$-stage Runge–Kutta branch for a $C^1$ parameter-dependent vector field $f(t,y,\theta)$. Let $F(Y,u,\theta)$ be the stack of its stage evaluations and
$$G(Y,u,\theta)=Y-\mathbf1\otimes u-h(A\otimes I_d)F(Y,u,\theta).$$
Assume the branch is the unique root in the invariant ball of [[lem-small-step-implicit-rk-branch-and-residual-error]], and its stage derivative $G_Y$ obeys the hypotheses of [[lem-implicit-rk-stage-jacobian-nonsingular-on-branch]]. Then the branch $Y(\theta)$ is locally $C^1$ and
$$D_\theta Y=-G_Y^{-1}\bigl(G_uD_\theta u+G_\theta\bigr).$$
For the update $\Psi_h(u,\theta)=u+h(\mathbf1^T_b\otimes I_d)F(Y(\theta),u(\theta),\theta)$,
$$D_\theta\Psi_h=D_\theta u+h(b^T\otimes I_d)\bigl(F_YD_\theta Y+F_uD_\theta u+F_\theta\bigr).$$
These are exact derivatives of the selected algebraic stage branch. A finite-budget stage iteration is a different map and is not covered by this formula.

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: By [F2], the stated root exists on the selected ball, and [F4] makes $G_Y$ invertible there. Regard $R(\theta,Y)=G(Y,u(\theta),\theta)$. Its parameter derivative is $R_\theta=G_uD_\theta u+G_\theta$. Apply [F3] to obtain the local branch and the displayed formula for $D_\theta Y$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, A1]

review_basis.full_actual_interface:
Let $n,d\ge1$, let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0},P)$ be a discrete filtered probability space, and fix $k$. Let $f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be continuously differentiable, let $x:\Omega\to\mathbb R^d$ be $\mathcal F_k$-measurable, and suppose each $g_i=\nabla f_i(x)$ is square-integrable. Define $F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i$, $\bar g=n^{-1}\sum_i g_i=\nabla F(x)$ by [[lem-finite-sum-gradient-is-average]], and

$$
\sigma^2(x)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|g_i-\bar g\|_2^2.
$$

For an integer $b\ge1$, draw $I_1,\ldots,I_b$ as mutually independent uniform indices from $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with the whole index vector independent of $\mathcal F_k$, and set $G_b=b^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^b g_{I_j}$. Then

$$\mathbb E[G_b\mid\mathcal F_k]=\bar g,\qquad \mathbb E[\|G_b-\bar g\|_2^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=\frac{\sigma^2(x)}b.$$

For sampling without replacement, let $S$ be a uniform subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ of size $b$, independent of $\mathcal F_k$, and set $G_S=b^{-1}\sum_{i\in S}g_i$. If $n>1$ and $1\le b\le n$, then

$$\mathbb E[G_S\mid\mathcal F_k]=\bar g,\qquad \mathbb E[\|G_S-\bar g\|_2^2\mid\mathcal F_k] =\frac{n-b}{b(n-1)}\sigma^2(x).$$

When $n=1$, the without-replacement case requires $b=1$; both estimators equal $\bar g$ and both errors are zero.

review_basis.full_actual_interface:
For the semi-explicit DAE with $x\in\mathbb R^d$, $z\in\mathbb R^m$, and $d,m\ge1$, let $x'=F(t,x)$ be the reduced ODE from [[thm-index-one-dae-implicit-function-reduction]] on $[0,T]$, with exact solution $\bar x\in C^2$. Suppose all exact and numerical states lie in a common compact branch tube, $F$ is Lipschitz in $x$ there with constant $L$, $\psi$ is Lipschitz in $x$ with constant $L_\psi$, and $f$ is Lipschitz in $z$ with constant $L_z$. Assume the residual lemma's hypotheses hold uniformly on this tube: there are common $\gamma>0$, $\Lambda\ge0$, and $\rho>0$ for its lower singular-value and Jacobian-Lipschitz bounds at every base point, with $\rho\le\gamma/(\sqrt m\,\Lambda)$ when $\Lambda>0$; all numerical algebraic candidates lie in the corresponding balls $B(\psi(t_n,X_n),\rho)$. Use a uniform grid $t_n=nh$, $h=T/N$, $T>0$, and $N\ge1$. Assume the starting pair also lies in its branch ball and

$$
\|X_0-\bar x(0)\|_2\le C_0h,\qquad \|g(0,X_0,Z_0)\|_2\le C_{a,0}h.
$$

For each $1\le n\le N$, suppose $(X_n,Z_n)$ lies in the branch ball and its coupled backward-Euler residuals satisfy

$$
r^d_n=\frac{X_n-X_{n-1}}h-f(t_n,X_n,Z_n),\quad r^a_n=g(t_n,X_n,Z_n),\quad \|r^d_n\|_2\le C_dh,\quad \|r^a_n\|_2\le C_ah.
$$

Then a constant $C$, independent of $h$, satisfies

$$
\max_{0\le n\le N}\Bigl(\|X_n-\bar x(t_n)\|_2+\|Z_n-\psi(t_n,\bar x(t_n))\|_2\Bigr)\le Ch
$$

for all sufficiently small $h$. This is a conditional accuracy result for accepted residuals; the finite-budget solver may return a failure status.

Suppose all exact and numerical states lie in a common compact branch tube, $F$ is Lipschitz in $x$ there with constant $L$, $\psi$ is Lipschitz in $x$ with constant $L_\psi$, and $f$ is Lipschitz in $z$ with constant $L_z$. Assume the residual lemma's hypotheses hold uniformly on this tube: there are common $\gamma>0$, $\Lambda\ge0$, and $\rho>0$ for its lower singular-value and Jacobian-Lipschitz bounds at every base point, with $\rho\le\gamma/(\sqrt m\,\Lambda)$ when $\Lambda>0$; all numerical algebraic candidates lie in the corresponding balls $B(\psi(t_n,X_n),\rho)$. Use a uniform grid $t_n=nh$, $h=T/N$, $T>0$, and $N\ge1$. Assume the starting pair also lies in its branch ball and

$$
\|X_0-\bar x(0)\|_2\le C_0h,\qquad \|g(0,X_0,Z_0)\|_2\le C_{a,0}h.
$$

For each $1\le n\le N$, suppose $(X_n,Z_n)$ lies in the branch ball and its coupled backward-Euler residuals satisfy

$$
r^d_n=\frac{X_n-X_{n-1}}h-f(t_n,X_n,Z_n),\quad r^a_n=g(t_n,X_n,Z_n),\quad \|r^d_n\|_2\le C_dh,\quad \|r^a_n\|_2\le C_ah.
$$

Then a constant $C$, independent of $h$, satisfies

$$
\max_{0\le n\le N}\Bigl(\|X_n-\bar x(t_n)\|_2+\|Z_n-\psi(t_n,\bar x(t_n))\|_2\Bigr)\le Ch
$$

for all sufficiently small $h$. This is a conditional accuracy result for accepted residuals; the finite-budget solver may return a failure status.

Assume $F$ is Lipschitz in $x$ on a common compact tube with constant $L$, $\psi$ is Lipschitz in $x$ there with constant $L_\psi$, $f$ is Lipschitz in $z$ with constant $L_z$, and the residual lemma's hypotheses hold uniformly on this tube: common $\gamma>0$, $\Lambda\ge0$, and $\rho>0$ in its lower singular-value and Jacobian-Lipschitz bounds, with $\rho\le\gamma/(\sqrt m\,\Lambda)$ when $\Lambda>0$. $$
\|X_j-\bar x(t_j)\|_2\le C_sh^2,\qquad \|g(t_j,X_j,Z_j)\|_2\le C_{a,s}h^2,\qquad j=0,1.
$$

For each $2\le n\le N$, suppose the constant-step BDF2 derivative and algebraic residuals satisfy

$$
r^d_n=\frac{3X_n-4X_{n-1}+X_{n-2}}{2h}-f(t_n,X_n,Z_n),\quad r^a_n=g(t_n,X_n,Z_n),\quad \|r^d_n\|_2\le C_dh^2,\quad \|r^a_n\|_2\le C_ah^2.

$$
\max_{0\le n\le N}\Bigl(\|X_n-\bar x(t_n)\|_2+\|Z_n-\psi(t_n,\bar x(t_n))\|_2\Bigr)\le Ch^2.
$$

The starter hypothesis holds, in particular, for an exact consistent $X_0,Z_0$ and one backward-Euler startup from $X_0$ with derivative residual $O(h)$ and algebraic residual $O(h^2)$. Assume $F$ is Lipschitz in $x$ on a common compact tube with constant $L$, $\psi$ is Lipschitz in $x$ there with constant $L_\psi$, $f$ is Lipschitz in $z$ with constant $L_z$, and the residual lemma's hypotheses hold uniformly on this tube: common $\gamma>0$, $\Lambda\ge0$, and $\rho>0$ in its lower singular-value and Jacobian-Lipschitz bounds, with $\rho\le\gamma/(\sqrt m\,\Lambda)$ when $\Lambda>0$. Every numerical algebraic candidate lies in its corresponding branch ball. Use a constant grid $t_n=nh$, $h=T/N$, $T>0$, and $N\ge2$. Suppose the two starting pairs satisfy

$$
\|X_j-\bar x(t_j)\|_2\le C_sh^2,\qquad \|g(t_j,X_j,Z_j)\|_2\le C_{a,s}h^2,\qquad j=0,1.
$$

For each $2\le n\le N$, suppose the constant-step BDF2 derivative and algebraic residuals satisfy

$$
r^d_n=\frac{3X_n-4X_{n-1}+X_{n-2}}{2h}-f(t_n,X_n,Z_n),\quad r^a_n=g(t_n,X_n,Z_n),\quad \|r^d_n\|_2\le C_dh^2,\quad \|r^a_n\|_2\le C_ah^2.
$$

Then, for all sufficiently small $h$, a constant $C$ independent of $h$ satisfies

$$
\max_{0\le n\le N}\Bigl(\|X_n-\bar x(t_n)\|_2+\|Z_n-\psi(t_n,\bar x(t_n))\|_2\Bigr)\le Ch^2.
$$

The starter hypothesis holds, in particular, for an exact consistent $X_0,Z_0$ and one backward-Euler startup from $X_0$ with derivative residual $O(h)$ and algebraic residual $O(h^2)$. The error theorem is conditional on the residual bounds and selected branch; it does not assert that a finite Newton budget meets them.

review_basis.full_actual_interface:
In the exact-arithmetic model with returning residual, Jacobian, domain-test and correction primitives, suppose the initialization and stepper algorithms in [[alg-index-one-dae-consistent-initialization]], [[alg-index-one-dae-backward-euler-stepper]], and [[alg-index-one-dae-bdf2-stepper]] are run with finite grid length and finite Newton budget $B$. Count explicit residual queries separately from work internal to Jacobian assembly and linear-system backends. Each call returns a status after finitely many such queries. A Newton call makes at most $B$ correction calls and $B+1$ explicit residual evaluations. Initialization makes at most one additional algebraic-residual evaluation after a root status to record the returned residual norm, so it uses at most $B+2$ evaluations. A backward-Euler call with $S$ attempted steps uses at most $1+S(B+2)$ residual evaluations, including its one starting algebraic-residual check; a BDF2 call with $S$ attempted steps uses at most $2+S(B+2)$, including its two starting algebraic-residual checks. These bounds include calls that return early with a failure status. Every successful correction solves one current Jacobian system, of dimension $m$ in initialization and $d+m$ in either stepper; assembly and solve costs depend on the backend.

For either stepper, every appended candidate satisfies $\|r^d_n\|_2\le\eta_d$ and $\|r^a_n\|_2\le\eta_a$ for its defined derivative and algebraic residuals. These are conditional accepted-residual bounds. No residual tolerance is guaranteed to be attained, and these bounds assert neither an exact zero, uniqueness nor a discretization error estimate.

Let $d,m\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R^d$, $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^k$ for $k\ge1$. Suppose $g(t_*,x_*,z_*)=0$ and $g_z(t_*,x_*,z_*)$ is invertible. Then there are neighborhoods $U$ of $(t_*,x_*)$ and $V$ of $z_*$, and a unique $C^k$ map $\psi:U\to V$, such that, for $(t,x)\in U$ and $z\in V$,

$$
g(t,x,z)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad z=\psi(t,x).
$$

Its derivatives satisfy

$$
\psi_t=-g_z^{-1}g_t,\qquad \psi_x=-g_z^{-1}g_x,
$$

with the derivatives of $g$ evaluated at $(t,x,\psi(t,x))$. The reduced vector field $F(t,x)=f(t,x,\psi(t,x))$ is $C^k$ on $U$. Thus solutions of the DAE that stay in this selected chart are exactly solutions of $x'=F(t,x)$ paired with $z=\psi(t,x)$.

proofparagraphs.text: Subtract the equations for $\eta_t$ and $q_t$ and add and subtract $F_\Delta(q_t)$. The vector-field term is bounded by $C_Td_{BL}(\eta_t,q_t)$ using [F5]; the residual is at most $r:=C_Q\Delta$ by [F3]. Therefore $d(t)\le C_T\int_0^td(s)ds+rt$, with $d(0)=0$. source_evidence.full_current_interface: If [[alg-interval-hermitian-ldl-inertia-certifier]] returns `certified-inertia` with $(n_+,n_-,n_0)$, every Hermitian matrix in its input family has exactly that inertia. A `pivot-inconclusive` return does not imply that any family member is singular.
source_evidence.item_specific_mathematical_focus: A certified inertia return is uniform over the Hermitian family; an inconclusive pivot is not evidence that the family contains a singular member.
selected_current_proof_blocks: 1.1 Induct over the pivot blocks. Initially the active interval matrix encloses each permuted family member. If this holds before a block, [F1] makes the outward inverse and update enclose that member's exact pivot inverse and Schur complement; [F4] ensures the pivot is nonsingular throughout the family. Hence the enclosure invariant holds at the next block. By [F3] the initial permutation has not changed any inertia. [given, F1, F3, F4, induction]

2.1 A certified one-by-one pivot has the sign of its real interval. By [F5], each accepted two-by-two pivot has exactly its reported inertia. Applying [F2] successively to each pivot and its Schur complement proves that the sum returned at completion is the inertia of every original family member. If a test is unresolved the algorithm returns no inertia claim, and failure alone supplies no singularity conclusion. [F2, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

2.1 A certified one-by-one pivot has the sign of its real interval. By [F5], each accepted two-by-two pivot has exactly its reported inertia. If a test is unresolved the algorithm returns no inertia claim, and failure alone supplies no singularity conclusion. [F2, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume AC. Let $X,Y$ be Hilbert spaces over the same field
$\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and let $F:U\to Y$ be continuously
Fréchet differentiable over $\mathbb F$ on open $U\subseteq X$. In the
complex case, each $F'(x)$ is a bounded complex-linear operator and the
Fréchet remainder is measured over complex increments. Let
$B=\overline B(x^\dagger,\rho)\subseteq U$, with $\rho>0$, and
$y=F(x^\dagger)$. Set $A=F'(x^\dagger)$, $S=A^*A$. Suppose $F'$ is
Lipschitz on $B$ and, for every $x\in B$,
$$F'(x)=(I+R_x)A,\qquad \|R_x\|\le\kappa<1/5,\qquad \kappa\ge0,$$
with bounded linear $R_x:Y\to Y$ and $R_{x^\dagger}=0$. This is an explicit additional weak-nonlinearity hypothesis; it is not inferred from the original tangential-cone/Lipschitz assumptions alone.

Suppose $e_0=x_0-x^\dagger=S^\nu w$, $0<\nu\le1/2$, $\|w\|\le W$, where $W>0$; changing the sign of $w$ gives the original opposite-sign source convention. Let $\alpha_0>0$, $\alpha_0\ge\|A\|^2$, $0<q<1$, and $\alpha_k=\alpha_0q^k$. Define
$$\beta=\nu+1/2,\quad \theta=2\kappa+\kappa^2,\quad d_0=2\kappa(1+\kappa),\quad c_0=1+\kappa,$$
$$a=(1-\theta)^{-1},\quad b=d_0/(1-\theta),\quad c=c_0/(1-\theta),\qquad b<q^\beta,$$
$$D=\max\{1,a/(q^\beta-b)\},\quad E=c/(1-b),\quad C_e=1+D(d_0+\theta q^\beta)/2,\quad N_e=[c_0+(d_0+\theta)E]/2.$$
Require the source-smallness and discrepancy conditions
$$(C_e+N_e)W\alpha_0^\nu<\rho,\qquad \tau>(1+\kappa)(D+E)+1.$$
For each $0<\delta<W\alpha_0^\beta$ and datum $\|y_\delta-y\|\le\delta$, use the **anchored** recurrence of [[alg-anchored-irgnm-with-discrepancy-stopping]]. Its theoretical exact extension, ignoring the stopping tests, is well-defined and lies in $B$ through
$$K_\delta=\min\{k\ge0:W\alpha_k^\beta\le\delta\}.$$
Its first ordinary discrepancy crossing $k_\delta=\min\{k:\|F(x_k^\delta)-y_\delta\|\le\tau\delta\}$ is finite and $k_\delta\le K_\delta$. For the theoretical extension through this comparison index,
$$\|A(x_k^\delta-x^\dagger)\|\le DW\alpha_k^\beta+E\delta,\qquad \|x_{k+1}^\delta-x^\dagger\|\le C_eW\alpha_k^\nu+N_e\delta/\sqrt{\alpha_k}\quad(0\le k<K_\delta).$$
As $\delta\downarrow0$, $x_{k_\delta}^\delta\to x^\dagger$ in norm for every admissible noise sequence. For exact data the extended recurrence converges to $x^\dagger$ as well. A finite actual algorithm returns this first-crossing iterate only if its cap reaches $k_\delta$ and exact calls succeed; shorter caps and uncertified calls retain their explicit failure statuses. No nonlinear rate is asserted, and no injectivity, closed range or finite-dimensional restriction on $A$ is imposed. The retained unanchored LM algorithm is not claimed to satisfy this anchored theorem.

source_evidence.full_current_interface:
Let $n\ge1$, let $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ and $\mathcal b\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ be nonempty, let $X$ be a nonempty closed complex rectangle box in $\mathbb C^n\cong\mathbb R^{2n}$, let $x_0\in X$, and let the point matrix $R$ be nonsingular. For each fixed $A\in\mathcal A,b\in\mathcal b$, define
$$
\Phi_{A,b}(x)=x-R(Ax-b)
$$
and
$$
K^*(X)=\{x_0-R(Ax_0-b)+(I-RA)(x-x_0): A\in\mathcal A,\ b\in\mathcal b,\ x\in X\}.
$$
If $K^*(X)\subseteq X$, then every admitted pair $(A,b)$ has a solution in $X$. If in addition a number $q<1$ satisfies $\|I-RA\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}\le q$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$, that solution is unique in $X$ for each fixed pair.
source_evidence.item_specific_mathematical_focus: Set inclusion for the whole matrix/right-hand-side family gives existence in the supplied box; a separate strict contraction bound gives uniqueness for each fixed pair.
selected_current_proof_blocks: 1.1 Fix any $A\in\mathcal A,b\in\mathcal b$. Algebra gives $\Phi_{A,b}(x)=x_0-R(Ax_0-b)+(I-RA)(x-x_0)$, so $K^*(X)\subseteq X$ implies $\Phi_{A,b}(X)\subseteq X$. The affine map $\Phi_{A,b}$ is continuous on the closed box, so [F1] gives a fixed point $x\in X$. Since $R$ is nonsingular, $\Phi_{A,b}(x)=x$ is equivalent to $Ax=b$. [given, F1, algebra]

review_basis.full_actual_interface:
Let $n\ge1$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have continuous second partial derivatives ($C^2$), let $x_0\in\mathbb R^n$, and set $L_0:=\{x:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}$. Assume $L_0$ is convex, contains a global minimizer $x_*$, and for every $x\in L_0$ the symmetric Hessian $G(x):=\nabla^2 f(x)$ satisfies $\mu\|v\|_2^2\le v^TG(x)v$ and $\|G(x)\|_2\le\Lambda$ for some $0<\mu\le\Lambda<\infty$. Fix $0<c_1<c_2<1/2$ for the line searches. Fix a memory length $m_{\rm mem}\ge1$ and run the exact-arithmetic limited-memory algorithm of [[alg-lbfgs-two-loop-with-curvature-filter]] with successful strong Wolfe searches. Suppose every stored pair satisfies, for constants $0<a\le b<\infty$ and $C>0$,
$$ a\|s_i\|_2^2\le s_i^Ty_i\le b\|s_i\|_2^2, \qquad \frac{\|y_i\|_2^2}{s_i^Ty_i}\le C, $$
and every base scale lies in $[\gamma_{\min},\gamma_{\max}]$ with $0<\gamma_{\min}\le\gamma_{\max}<\infty$. Let $\underline\lambda,\overline\lambda$ be the explicit constants from [[lem-lbfgs-curvature-bounds-imply-uniform-spectrum]], and set
$$ \kappa:=\frac{2\mu c_1(1-c_2)\underline\lambda^2} {\Lambda\overline\lambda^2}\in(0,1). $$
Then for every generated iterate
$$ f(x_k)-f(x_*)\le(1-\kappa)^k[f(x_0)-f(x_*)], \qquad \|x_k-x_*\|_2\le\sqrt{\frac{2[f(x_0)-f(x_*)]}{\mu}}\,(1-\kappa)^{k/2}. $$
In an infinite successful continuation, the gradient norms tend to zero and the iterates converge with the displayed geometric error bound; any finite-budget stop is only a prefix. The pair and scale bounds are hypotheses; positive curvature alone does not imply them.
review_basis.source_specific_focus: Uniform secant/scale bounds give a fixed positive inverse spectrum and the displayed geometric objective and iterate-error bounds for successful limited-memory steps.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $s\ge0$, $N\ge0$, and $u=\sum_{n\ge0}c_nP_n\in H_L^s$ from [[def-legendre-weighted-sobolev-scale]]. Then
$$
\|u-\Pi_Nu\|_{L_L^2}\le(1+(N+1)(N+2))^{-s/2}\|u\|_{H_L^s}.
$$

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: For a finite Legendre sum, [F1] gives $u-\Pi_Nu=\sum_{n>N}c_nP_n$. Orthogonality [F2] therefore gives $\|u-\Pi_Nu\|_{L_L^2}^2=\sum_{n>N}\frac{2}{2n+1}|c_n|^2.$ For every $n>N$, $1+n(n+1)\ge1+(N+1)(N+2)$; multiplying each term by the inverse weight gives the stated squared bound for finite sums. [F1, F2, algebra]
actualproofparagraphs.2.1: Finite sums are dense in the completion defining $H_L^s$. The truncation $\Pi_N$ is contractive in both the coefficient norm and the $s=0$ norm, so the finite-sum inequality passes to the limit along any Cauchy sequence of finite sums. Taking square roots proves the claimed estimate for every $u\in H_L^s$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $P\in\mathcal P_r$ and let $F=F(P)$ be Hermitian. Define the level-shifted
matrix $F_s=F+s(I-P)$ for real $s$, and define the Hermitian compressions
$$F_{occ}:=(PFP)|_{\operatorname{ran}P},\qquad F_{vir}:=((I-P)F(I-P))|_{\operatorname{ran}(I-P)}.$$
For either finite-dimensional Hermitian block, $\sigma$ denotes its finite
eigenvalue set. When $PF=FP$, these compressions are the restrictions of $F$
to the two invariant subspaces. Then
$$\Pi_r(F_s)=P$$
if and only if $PF=FP$ and
$$\max\sigma(F_{occ})<\min\sigma(F_{vir})+s.$$
The strict inequality is the shifted occupied/unoccupied ordering. A level shift
can change the map when either commutation or this ordering fails.

Assume the hypotheses of [[def-regular-holonomic-phase-space-and-dynamics]] on a compact regular chart $K$. For every consistent initial pair $(q_0,p_0)\in\mathcal M$ with $q_0\in K$ there is a unique local solution of
$$\dot q=M^{-1}p,\qquad \dot p=-\nabla V(q)-J(q)^T\lambda(q,p),$$

proofparagraphs.text: Since $J(q)$ has full row rank and $M^{-1}$ is SPD, for every nonzero $\eta\in\mathbb R^m$ we have $\eta^TA(q)\eta=(J(q)^T\eta)^TM^{-1}(J(q)^T\eta)>0$. Thus $A(q)$ is invertible; its entries are smooth and $A^{-1}=\operatorname{adj}(A)/\det A$, so its inverse and the displayed multiplier are smooth on a neighborhood of the chart. [F1, algebra]

additional_source_clauses.text:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, let $c:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be smooth (that is, $C^\infty$) with $1\le m<d$, let $M$ be a constant symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix, and let $V:U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. A **holonomic constraint** is the position condition $c(q)=0$. Write $J(q)=Dc(q)$, let $Q=\{q\in U:c(q)=0\}$, and define its regular part by $Q_{\mathrm{reg}}=\{q\in Q:\operatorname{rank}J(q)=m\}$. For $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A(q)=J(q)M^{-1}J(q)^T$ is positive definite. On a compact regular chart $K\subset Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A^{-1}$ is uniformly bounded: $\sup_{q\in K}\|A(q)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty$.

A position-momentum pair $(q,p)$ is **consistent** when $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$. The **regular constrained phase manifold** is
$$\mathcal M=\{(q,p)\in U\times\mathbb R^d:c(q)=0,\ J(q)M^{-1}p=0,\ q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}\}.$$
The ambient canonical two-form is $\omega_0=\sum_{i=1}^d dq_i\wedge dp_i$; its restriction to $\mathcal M$ is denoted $\omega_{\mathcal M}$.

For $v=M^{-1}p$, the constrained Hamilton equations are
$$\dot q=v,\qquad \dot p=-\nabla V(q)-J(q)^T\lambda,$$
with multiplier
$$\lambda=A(q)^{-1}\bigl(D^2c(q)[v,v]-J(q)M^{-1}\nabla V(q)\bigr).$$
Here $D^2c(q)[v,v]\in\mathbb R^m$ has components $v^TD^2c_j(q)v$. This multiplier is the one that keeps both $c(q)=0$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$ satisfied.

Suppose a validated ordered eigenvalue enclosure certifies index one with gap $\gamma>0$ in the sense of [[def-validated-eigenvalue-enclosures-for-an-index-one-hessian]]. If $\epsilon_g=0$, then $x$ is an exact critical point with Hessian index one.

If $\epsilon_g>0$, put $\rho=2\epsilon_g/\gamma$. Assume $B_2(x,2\rho)\subset U$, the Hessian is $L$-Lipschitz there, and $L\rho/\gamma\le1/2$. Then there is exactly one critical point $x_*$ in $\overline B_2(x,\rho)$, it satisfies $\|x_*-x\|_2\le\rho$, and its Hessian has exactly one negative eigenvalue and no zero eigenvalues. The reported residual $\epsilon_g$, gap $\gamma$, conditioning bound $1/\gamma$, Hessian Lipschitz constant $L$, and radius condition are part of the certificate; a residual or a Ritz value alone is not a certificate.

source_evidence.full_current_interface:
Let $A$ be maximal monotone on $E=\mathbb R^n$ and let $\rho>0$. For every
$y\in E$ there is a unique $x\in E$ with $y-x\in\rho A(x)$. Thus the
resolvent from [[def-resolvent-of-a-monotone-relation]] is an everywhere-defined
map and, for all $y,y'\in E$,
$$\|J_{\rho A}y-J_{\rho A}y'\|_2^2\le \langle J_{\rho A}y-J_{\rho A}y',y-y'\rangle.$$
This is firm nonexpansiveness; it also implies the map is 1-Lipschitz.

Set $\tilde x=(y+q)/2$ and $\tilde a=(y-q)/(2\rho)$. selected_current_proof_blocks: 1.1 Transform every graph pair $(x,a)\in A$ into $p=x+\rho a$ and $q=x-\rho a$. Also, if $p=p'$, this inequality forces $q=q'$. Thus the rule $T(p)=q$ is a well-defined 1-Lipschitz map on its range $D=\{x+\rho a:(x,a)\in A\}$. [A1, F1, construct, algebra]

3.1 If $x,x'$ both satisfy $y-x\in\rho A(x)$ and $y-x'\in\rho A(x')$, monotonicity gives $0\le\langle x-x',(y-x)-(y-x')\rangle=-\|x-x'\|_2^2$. Thus $x=x'$, so the resolvent is single-valued. [A1, F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

literal_source_anchor.description: the finite correction iteration including its first/final recurrence
literal_source_anchor.quote: Write $b_q:=\frac{B_qh^q}{q!}(f^{(q-1)}(b)-f^{(q-1)}(a))$ for $q\ge2$. If $k+1$ is odd and at least $3$, [F2] makes that boundary term zero, so step 1.2 gives $J_k=-J_{k+1}$. If $k+1=2r$ is even, step 1.2 gives $J_{2r-1}=b_{2r}-J_{2r}$. For each $r<p$, the odd-index recurrence at $k=2r$ gives $J_{2r}=-J_{2r+1}$; hence $J_{2r-1}=b_{2r}+J_{2r+1}$. Finite induction on $r=1,\ldots,p-1$ ([[thm-induction-principle]]) iterates these identities; followed by the final even-index recurrence, it gives $J_1=\sum_{r=1}^{p}\frac{B_{2r}h^{2r}}{(2r)!}\bigl(f^{(2r-1)}(b)-f^{(2r-1)}(a)\bigr)-J_{2p}.$ [given, step 1.2, F2, algebra]

literal_source_anchor.description: the closed-interval smooth expansion and supplied trapezoid-table hypotheses
literal_source_anchor.quote:
Let $a<b$, let $m\ge1$ and $L\ge m$ be integers, and let $f\in C^{2m+2}([a,b])$. Write $h_\ell=(b-a)2^{-\ell}$ and let $(R_{\ell,j})$ be the table from [[alg-na-romberg-trapezoid-table]]. If the trapezoid expansion has coefficients $c_1,\ldots,c_m$ as in [[cor-na-composite-trapezoid-even-power-expansion]], then the recurrence cancels all first $m$ even powers and there is a finite $C_{m,L}$ such that
$$|R_{L,m}-\int_a^b f(x)\,dx|\le C_{m,L}h_L^{2m+2}.$$
No error-order conclusion is made from a ratio of observed consecutive trapezoid errors.

source_evidence.full_current_interface:
Let $n\ge1$ and let $(V,\Theta,\delta,\rho,M_A,M_\Theta,\tau)$ be a residual and orthogonality certificate for a nonempty family $\mathcal A$ of Hermitian matrices in $\mathbb C^{n\times n}$. Sort the diagonal entries of $\Theta$ increasingly as $\theta_{(1)}\le\cdots\le\theta_{(n)}$. Then every $A\in\mathcal A$ has ordered eigenvalues $\lambda_1(A)\le\cdots\le\lambda_n(A)$ satisfying
$$
|\lambda_k(A)-\theta_{(k)}|\le \rho+(M_A+M_\Theta)\tau,\qquad 1\le k\le n.
$$

source_evidence.full_current_interface:
Let $n\ge1$ and let $(V,\Theta,\delta,\rho,M_A,M_\Theta,\tau)$ be a residual and orthogonality certificate for a nonempty family $\mathcal A$ of Hermitian matrices in $\mathbb C^{n\times n}$. Sort the diagonal entries of $\Theta$ increasingly as $\theta_{(1)}\le\cdots\le\theta_{(n)}$. Then every $A\in\mathcal A$ has ordered eigenvalues $\lambda_1(A)\le\cdots\le\lambda_n(A)$ satisfying
$$
|\lambda_k(A)-\theta_{(k)}|\le \rho+(M_A+M_\Theta)\tau,\qquad 1\le k\le n.
$$
source_evidence.item_specific_mathematical_focus: A residual/orthogonality certificate gives uniform ordered Hermitian eigenvalue intervals after sorting the approximate diagonal values.
selected_current_proof_blocks: 2.1 Set $Q=VH^{-1}$. Then $Q^*Q=H^{-1}V^*VH^{-1}=I$. Thus $Q$ is injective and [F4] makes the square matrix $Q$ invertible, so $Q$ is unitary. The eigenvalues of $H$ lie between $\sqrt{1-\delta}$ and $\sqrt{1+\delta}$, hence $\|V-Q\|_2=\|Q(H-I)\|_2=\|H-I\|_2\le1-\sqrt{1-\delta}\le\tau$. For the upper deviation, $\sqrt{1+\delta}-1\le1-\sqrt{1-\delta}$ because $\sqrt{1+\delta}+\sqrt{1-\delta}\le2$. Unitary invariance in [F5] justifies the norm equality. [given, F1, F2, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For each $A\in\mathcal A$, the residual identity $AQ-Q\Theta=A(Q-V)+(AV-V\Theta)+(V-Q)\Theta$ and certificate bounds give $\|AQ-Q\Theta\|_2\le M_A\tau+\rho+\tau M_\Theta=\eta$. By the triangle inequality and submultiplicativity [F7], each product term in the identity is bounded by its factor norms, giving the displayed estimate. Since $Q$ is unitary, [F5] gives that $Q^*AQ$ has the same ordered eigenvalues as $A$ and, using [F7], $\|Q^*AQ-\Theta\|_2=\|Q^*(AQ-Q\Theta)\|_2\le\eta$. [given, F5, F7, step 2.1, algebra]

source_evidence.full_current_interface: Let an exact nonconstant phase-fixed periodic orbit and monodromy matrix $M_*$ be supplied by a sound periodic-orbit certificate. Suppose $M_*$ belongs to a matrix family with a certified complete cluster list of pairwise disjoint filled convex polygons $P_0,\ldots,P_s$: each count is certified by [[thm-floquet-multiplier-cluster-certificate-soundness]], the counts sum to the state dimension $d$, $1\in\operatorname{int}P_0$, and the count in $P_0$ is one. Suppose also that for each $j\ge1$, $P_j\subset\{z:|z|\le1-\sigma\}$ for one supplied $\sigma>0$. Then the periodic orbit is orbitally asymptotically stable. If any non-phase cluster enclosure meets or intersects the unit circle, these hypotheses fail and this theorem gives no stability verdict.
source_evidence.item_specific_mathematical_focus: A complete disjoint polygon cluster list isolates one neutral phase multiplier and strictly contracts every remaining cluster, yielding orbital asymptotic stability.
selected_current_proof_blocks: 2.1 Nonconstancy and flow uniqueness [F6] imply $f(\gamma(0))\ne0$, since otherwise the constant solution through $\gamma(0)$ would be the unique trajectory. Define $H=\{t\in\mathbb R:\gamma(t)=\gamma(0)\}$. Flow uniqueness makes $H$ an additive subgroup: a return to $\gamma(0)$ repeats the entire trajectory, so sums and differences of return times are return times. Continuity makes $H$ closed. One coordinate has nonzero derivative at zero and is strictly monotone on a sufficiently short interval; hence $H$ has no nonzero element there. Its positive infimum $S$ is therefore positive and belongs to $H$ by closedness. For any positive period $T$, division by $S$ gives $T=kS+r$ with integer $k\ge1$ and $0\le r<S$; the subgroup property gives $r\in H$, so minimality forces $r=0$. Thus $T=kS$, where $S$ is the least positive period. [F1, F6, step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 Let $M_S$ be the monodromy over $S$. By flow composition and the chain rule [F6], $M_*=M_S^k$. The phase tangent is a $1$ eigenvector of $M_S$ by [F2]. If $M_Sv=\alpha v$ with $\alpha^k
e1$, then $M_*v=\alpha^kv$ is a non-phase eigenvalue of $M_*$, so step 1.1 gives $|\alpha|^k<1$ and $|\alpha|<1$. If $\alpha^k=1$ and $\alpha
e1$, then $v$ and the phase tangent are independent eigenvectors of $M_*$ for eigenvalue $1$, contradicting its algebraic simplicity. If $\alpha=1$ and there were an eigenvector independent of the phase tangent, the same contradiction follows. If the eigenvalue $1$ of $M_S$ had a nontrivial Jordan chain, [F6] gives a generalized vector $v$ with $(M_S-I)v=f(\gamma(0))$ after rescaling. Then $(M_* - I)v=(M_S^k-I)v=k f(\gamma(0))
e0$, contradicting the algebraic simplicity of $1$ for $M_*$. Hence $1$ is simple for $M_S$ and every other eigenvalue of $M_S$ is strictly inside the unit circle. [F2, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume Countable Choice, and use the real evolution triple $(V,H,V^*)$ of [[def-parameterized-parabolic-variational-problem]]. On an open parameter set $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, assume the state map $\theta\mapsto u_\theta$ is Fr\'echet differentiable into $W(0,T;V)$, with derivative $w_\eta$ in direction $\eta\in\mathbb R^m$. Assume, for every $v\in V$ and almost every $t$,
$$\langle w_\eta'(t),v\rangle+a_\theta(t;w_\eta(t),v)=\langle f_\theta'[\eta](t),v\rangle-a_\theta'[\eta](t;u_\theta(t),v),\qquad w_\eta(0)=u_{0,\theta}'[\eta].$$
Let $\phi:H\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, and let $L:[0,T]\times V\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be measurable in time and $C^1$ in $(u,\theta)$ for almost every time, with a common integrable majorant that justifies differentiating its time integral. Assume $D_u\phi$ is represented by an element of $H$ and $D_uL(t,u_\theta,\theta)\in V^*$ is square-integrable in time. Suppose the adjoint $p\in W(0,T;V)$ satisfies
$$-\langle p'(t),v\rangle+a_\theta(t;v,p(t))=D_uL(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)[v],\qquad p(T)=\nabla_H\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta).$$
Then for $j(\theta)=\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)+\int_0^T L(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)\,dt$,
$$D j(\theta)[\eta]=D_\theta\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)[\eta]+(p(0),u_{0,\theta}'[\eta])_H+\int_0^T\left(D_\theta L(t,u_\theta,\theta)[\eta]+\langle f_\theta'[\eta](t),p(t)\rangle-a_\theta'[\eta](t;u_\theta(t),p(t))\right)dt.$$
This is conditional on the displayed differentiable state and adjoint; it does not prove either exists. The adjoint form is transposed as shown, so symmetry of $a_\theta$ is not required.
source_evidence.case_anchor: The theorem assumes the differentiated state and adjoint equations and integrable bounds; it does not supply a derivative through a singular or nondifferentiable state branch.

literal_source_anchor.quote:
Let $V_h$ be a finite-dimensional conforming subspace of a real evolution
triple. Let $a(t;\cdot,\cdot):V_h\times V_h\to\mathbb R$ be real bilinear
and measurable in $t$ for each fixed pair. Assume there is one null set
$E\subset(0,T)$ outside which, with common constants $0\le M<\infty$ and
$\alpha>0$,
$$|a(t;v_h,w_h)|\le M\|v_h\|_V\|w_h\|_V,\qquad a(t;v_h,v_h)\ge\alpha\|v_h\|_V^2\qquad(v_h,w_h\in V_h).$$
Let $f\in L^2(0,T;V_h^*)$. Let
$u_h\in H^1(0,T;V_h)$ be the semidiscrete solution from
[[thm-parabolic-finite-dimensional-measurable-ode]]. On a finite partition
$0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, put $\tau_j=t_j-t_{j-1}$ and
$\tau_{\max}=\max_j\tau_j$. For the interval-averaged backward Euler values
$U^j$ from [[alg-parabolic-backward-euler-averaged-forms]], define
$e^j=U^j-u_h(t_j)$ and let $\widehat U$ be the affine reconstruction, with
$\overline U(t)=U^j$ on $(t_{j-1},t_j)$. Every step has a unique solution.
With
$$C_U=\|U^0\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\|f\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2,$$
the separate maximum and cumulative bounds are
$$\max_{0\le m\le N}\|U^m\|_H^2\le C_U,\qquad \sum_{j=1}^N\|U^j-U^{j-1}\|_H^2+ \alpha\sum_{j=1}^N\tau_j\|U^j\|_V^2\le C_U.$$
The reconstruction satisfies
$$\|\widehat U'\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2 \le2\|f\|_{L^2(V_h^*)}^2+2M^2\|\overline U\|_{L^2(V)}^2,$$
$$\|\widehat U-\overline U\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2 \le\frac{c_i^2\tau_{\max}}3 \sum_{j=1}^N\|U^j-U^{j-1}\|_H^2,$$
where $c_i=\|V\hookrightarrow H\|$. For the nodal error, define
$$C_e=\|e^0\|_H^2+ \frac{M^2}{\alpha}\tau_{\max}^2 \|u_h'\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h)}^2.$$
Then the error obeys the separate bounds
$$\max_{0\le m\le N}\|e^m\|_H^2\le C_e,\qquad \alpha\sum_{j=1}^N\tau_j\|e^j\|_V^2\le C_e.$$
Thus exact initial projection $U^0=u_h(0)$ gives first-order maximum nodal
error. The reconstruction estimates provide bounds for later compactness
arguments; they do not themselves assert compactness.

Let $V_h$ be a finite-dimensional conforming subspace of a real evolution
triple. Assume a time-independent real bilinear form $a$ is bounded by $M$
and coercive by $\alpha>0$, the load $f\in L^2(0,T;V_h^*)$, and the
partition and data of [[alg-parabolic-crank-nicolson-cg1]]. Every time step
has a unique solution and, with
$U^{\mathrm{mid},j}=(U^j+U^{j-1})/2$,
$$\max_{0\le m\le N}\|U^m\|_H^2\le C_U,\qquad \alpha\sum_{j=1}^N\tau_j\|U^{\mathrm{mid},j}\|_V^2\le C_U, \quad C_U:=\|U^0\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\|f\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2.$$
If the exact semidiscrete solution $u_h$ from
[[thm-parabolic-finite-dimensional-measurable-ode]] satisfies
$u_h\in H^2(0,T;V_h)$, meaning $u_h,u_h',u_h''\in L^2(0,T;V_h)$ with weak
time derivatives. Under this regularity assumption, set
$e^j=U^j-u_h(t_j)$, $\tau_{\max}=\max_j\tau_j$, and
$$C_e:=\|e^0\|_H^2+ \frac{M^2}{16\alpha}\tau_{\max}^4 \|u_h''\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h)}^2.$$
Then the error satisfies the separate bounds
$$\max_{0\le m\le N}\|e^m\|_H^2\le C_e,\qquad \alpha\sum_{j=1}^N\tau_j \left\|\frac{e^j+e^{j-1}}2\right\|_V^2\le C_e.$$
Thus exact initial projection $U^0=u_h(0)$ gives second-order maximum nodal
error. The regularity hypothesis is on the time-dependent semidiscrete
solution and is not implied by the method definition.

Assume Countable Choice and the differentiable state/adjoint setting of [[thm-parabolic-adjoint-gradient-sensitivity]]. Let $u,p$ and $u_h,p_h$ denote the continuous and semidiscrete state/adjoint pairs, with gradients $g,g_h$ given by that theorem and its finite-dimensional application. Assume $u,p\in H^1(0,T;V)$, the parabolic form and its parameter derivative are uniformly bounded, and the form is coercive with constant $\alpha>0$. Suppose the forward state and time-reversed adjoint both satisfy the hypotheses of [[thm-parabolic-semidiscrete-ritz-error-splitting-and-energy-bound]], with operator-norm $C^1$ comparison maps $P_{u,h}(t),P_{p,h}(t):V\to V_h$. For the state comparison map, set $\rho_u=P_{u,h}u-u$, $\vartheta_u=u_h-P_{u,h}u$, and
$$\mathcal R_u(t)(v_h)=(\rho_u'(t),v_h)_H+a_\theta(t;\rho_u(t),v_h),\qquad \rho_u'=P_{u,h}'(t)u+P_{u,h}(t)u'-u'.$$
In reverse time $s=T-t$, put $q(s)=p(T-s)$ and $\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)=P_{p,h}(T-s)$; define $\rho_p(s)=\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)-q(s)$, $\vartheta_p(s)=p_h(T-s)-\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)$, and $\mathcal R_p(s)(v_h)=(\rho_p'(s),v_h)_H+a_\theta(T-s;v_h,\rho_p(s))$. The projection product rule gives $\rho_p'=\widetilde P_{p,h}'q+\widetilde P_{p,h}q'-q'$, with $\widetilde P_{p,h}'(s)=-P_{p,h}'(T-s)$. The Ritz supplier gives, for $z=u,p$,
$$\|z-z_h\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}\le E_z:=\|\rho_z\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}+\alpha^{-1/2}\left(\|\vartheta_z(0)\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\|\mathcal R_z\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2\right)^{1/2},$$
where the adjoint's initial trace means its terminal trace in original time. In particular, $\mathcal R_z$ contains the derivative of the time-dependent projection; it cannot be dropped from this hypothesis.

For $\|\eta\|_2\le1$, assume $\|D_\theta f[\eta]\|_{L^2(V^*)}\le M_f$, $\|D_\theta a(t)[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le M_a$ a.e., and define $U_*:=\max(\|u\|_{L^2(V)},\|u_h\|_{L^2(V)})$, $P_*:=\max(\|p\|_{L^2(V)},\|p_h\|_{L^2(V)})$, $P_{0,*}:=\max(\|p(0)\|_H,\|p_h(0)\|_H)$, and $U_0':=\|D_\theta u_0\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,H)}$. Suppose the discrete direct-objective derivative differs from the continuous direct-objective derivative $D_\theta\phi+\int_0^T D_\theta L\,dt$ by at most $\varepsilon_J$ in $\Theta^*$; suppose also $\|D_\theta u_{0,h}-D_\theta u_0\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,H)}\le\varepsilon_0$, $\|D_\theta f_h-D_\theta f\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,L^2(V^*))}\le\varepsilon_f$, and $\|D_\theta a_h-D_\theta a\|_{L^\infty(0,T;\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,\mathcal L(V,V^*)))}\le\varepsilon_a$. Put $E_{p,0}=\|p_h(0)-p(0)\|_H$. Then
$$\|g_h-g\|_{(\mathbb R^m)^*}\le \varepsilon_J+U_0'E_{p,0}+P_{0,*}\varepsilon_0+M_fE_p+\varepsilon_fP_*+M_a(E_uP_*+U_*E_p)+\varepsilon_aU_*P_*.$$
The derivative-data and trace defects are additional assumptions; an energy estimate for the state alone does not imply this gradient bound.

In reverse time $s=T-t$, put $q(s)=p(T-s)$ and $\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)=P_{p,h}(T-s)$; define $\rho_p(s)=\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)-q(s)$, $\vartheta_p(s)=p_h(T-s)-\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)$, and $\mathcal R_p(s)(v_h)=(\rho_p'(s),v_h)_H+a_\theta(T-s;v_h,\rho_p(s))$. The projection product rule gives $\rho_p'=\widetilde P_{p,h}'q+\widetilde P_{p,h}q'-q'$, with $\widetilde P_{p,h}'(s)=-P_{p,h}'(T-s)$. The Ritz supplier gives, for $z=u,p$,
$$\|z-z_h\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}\le E_z:=\|\rho_z\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}+\alpha^{-1/2}\left(\|\vartheta_z(0)\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\|\mathcal R_z\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2\right)^{1/2},$$
where the adjoint's initial trace means its terminal trace in original time. In particular, $\mathcal R_z$ contains the derivative of the time-dependent projection; it cannot be dropped from this hypothesis.

For $\|\eta\|_2\le1$, assume $\|D_\theta f[\eta]\|_{L^2(V^*)}\le M_f$, $\|D_\theta a(t)[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le M_a$ a.e., and define $U_*:=\max(\|u\|_{L^2(V)},\|u_h\|_{L^2(V)})$, $P_*:=\max(\|p\|_{L^2(V)},\|p_h\|_{L^2(V)})$, $P_{0,*}:=\max(\|p(0)\|_H,\|p_h(0)\|_H)$, and $U_0':=\|D_\theta u_0\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,H)}$. Suppose the discrete direct-objective derivative differs from the continuous direct-objective derivative $D_\theta\phi+\int_0^T D_\theta L\,dt$ by at most $\varepsilon_J$ in $\Theta^*$; suppose also $\|D_\theta u_{0,h}-D_\theta u_0\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,H)}\le\varepsilon_0$, $\|D_\theta f_h-D_\theta f\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,L^2(V^*))}\le\varepsilon_f$, and $\|D_\theta a_h-D_\theta a\|_{L^\infty(0,T;\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,\mathcal L(V,V^*)))}\le\varepsilon_a$. Put $E_{p,0}=\|p_h(0)-p(0)\|_H$. Then
$$\|g_h-g\|_{(\mathbb R^m)^*}\le \varepsilon_J+U_0'E_{p,0}+P_{0,*}\varepsilon_0+M_fE_p+\varepsilon_fP_*+M_a(E_uP_*+U_*E_p)+\varepsilon_aU_*P_*.$$
The derivative-data and trace defects are additional assumptions; an energy estimate for the state alone does not imply this gradient bound.

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: For the forward state, the product rule [F3] gives $\rho_u'=P_{u,h}'u+P_{u,h}u'-u'$, so the residual in [F2] is exactly the one displayed in the Statement. Apply the energy estimate in [F2] to $\vartheta_u$; it gives $\|\vartheta_u\|_{L^2(V)}\le\alpha^{-1/2}(\|\vartheta_u(0)\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\|\mathcal R_u\|_{L^2(V_h^*)}^2)^{1/2}$. Since $u-u_h=-\rho_u-\vartheta_u$, the triangle inequality proves the stated $E_u$ bound. [A1, F2, F3, given, algebra]
actualproofparagraphs.2.1: Set $s=T-t$ and $q(s)=p(T-s)$. The backward adjoint equation becomes a forward parabolic variational equation with transposed form $a_\theta(T-s;v,w)$, which has the same boundedness and coercivity constants. The comparison $\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)=P_{p,h}(T-s)$ is operator-norm $C^1$ and $\widetilde P_{p,h}'(s)=-P_{p,h}'(T-s)$. By [F3], its residual contains $\widetilde P_{p,h}'q+\widetilde P_{p,h}q'-q'$; apply the energy estimate in [F2] and the splitting $p-p_h=-\rho_p-\vartheta_p$ to get the stated $E_p$ bound by the same triangle inequality as step 1.1. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1, construct]
actualproofparagraphs.4.1: For the form term, add and subtract $D_\theta a[u_h,p_h]$. Its derivative-data defect is at most $\varepsilon_aU_*P_*$. Split the exact derivative difference as $D_\theta a[u_h-u,p_h]+D_\theta a[u,p_h-p]$; Cauchy--Schwarz in time, the bound $\|D_\theta a[\eta]\|\le M_a$, and steps 1.1 and 2.1 give $M_a(E_uP_*+U_*E_p)$. Combine this with step 3.1 and take the supremum over $\|\eta\|_2\le1$ to obtain the displayed dual norm bound. [A1, F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, given, algebra] ∎
