literal_source_anchor.description: the definitions of P_h,rho,theta and the full variational residual
literal_source_anchor.quote:
Assume Countable Choice and the bounded polyhedral mesh setting, spaces,
form and data of [[thm-parabolic-fem-semidiscrete-existence-energy]]. Let $u$
be the continuous solution supplied by
[[thm-parabolic-variational-wellposedness-and-energy-stability]] on the same
evolution triple and let $u_h$ be the corresponding semidiscrete solution.
For this error identity, assume the additional regularity $u\in H^1(0,T;V)$,
meaning $u,u'\in L^2(0,T;V)$ with the unique continuous representative
supplied by [[lem-parabolic-projection-time-product-rule]]. Let
$P_h:V\to V_h$ be a fixed bounded linear
comparison map, define
$$\rho(t)=P_hu(t)-u(t),\qquad\theta(t)=u_h(t)-P_hu(t),$$
and let $\mathcal R_h(t)\in V_h^*$ be the full residual
$$\mathcal R_h(t)(v_h)=(\rho'(t),v_h)_H+a(t;\rho(t),v_h).$$
Then for almost every $t$ and every $v_h\in V_h$,
$$(\theta'(t),v_h)_H+a(t;\theta(t),v_h)=-\mathcal R_h(t)(v_h),$$
and for every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\|\theta(t)\|_H^2+\alpha\int_0^t\|\theta(s)\|_V^2ds \le\|\theta(0)\|_H^2+ \alpha^{-1}\int_0^t\|\mathcal R_h(s)\|_{V_h^*}^2ds.$$

The same identity and energy bound hold for an operator-norm $C^1$
time-dependent comparison map $P_h(t):V\to V_h$, with its time derivative
included in $\rho'$ as stated below. For a time-independent form and the
Ritz projection $P_h=R_h$ from
[[def-parabolic-ritz-projection]], Galerkin orthogonality makes
$a(\rho(t),v_h)=0$, so the residual is exactly
$(R_hu'(t)-u'(t),v_h)_H$. If a time-dependent comparison $P_h(t)$ is used,
it must be operator-norm $C^1$; then
$\rho'=P_h'(t)u+P_h(t)u'-u'$, including the projection-derivative term.
For a measurable time-dependent form with a fixed comparison map, no
orthogonality is inferred and the full displayed residual remains.

literal_source_anchor.description: the real separable Hilbert evolution setting, which permits the scalar triple
literal_source_anchor.quote:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $T>0$, let $V$ be a separable real Hilbert
space, and let $(V,H,V^*)$ be its real evolution triple. Suppose
$a(t;\cdot,\cdot):V\times V\to\mathbb R$ is bilinear and scalar measurable
for each fixed pair $v,w\in V$, and there is one null set outside which
$$|a(t;v,w)|\le M\|v\|_V\|w\|_V,\qquad a(t;v,v)\ge\alpha\|v\|_V^2$$
for all $v,w\in V$, with constants $M>0$ and $\alpha>0$. Let
$f\in L^2(0,T;V^*)$ and $u_0\in H$. Then there is a unique
$u\in W(0,T;V)$ with $u(0)=u_0$ and, for almost every $t$,
$$\langle u'(t),v\rangle_{V^*,V}+a(t;u(t),v) =\langle f(t),v\rangle_{V^*,V}\qquad(v\in V).$$
For every $t\in[0,T]$ it satisfies
$$\|u(t)\|_H^2+\alpha\int_0^t\|u(s)\|_V^2\,ds \le\|u_0\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\int_0^t\|f(s)\|_{V^*}^2\,ds.$$
The proof applies BNB to the space-time form. Scalar measurability suffices
because $V$ is separable and the measurable inverse action is proved locally.

source_evidence.full_current_interface:
Assume the hypotheses of [[alg-pdhg-primal-dual-hybrid-gradient]] and that
$\Phi(x,y)=f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y)$ has a saddle point
$(x_*,y_*)$ in the sense of
[[def-saddle-point-for-convex-concave-lagrangian]]. For $N\ge1$ define
$$\bar x_N=\frac1N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}x^{k+1},\qquad \bar y_N=\frac1N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}y^{k+1}.$$
For every $x\in\operatorname{dom}f$, $y\in\operatorname{dom}g^*$,
$$\Phi(\bar x_N,y)-\Phi(x,\bar y_N) \le\frac1N\left(\frac{\|x-x^0\|_2^2}{2\tau} +\frac{\|y-y^0\|_2^2}{2\sigma}\right).$$
In particular, the saddle gap
$\Phi(\bar x_N,y_*)-\Phi(x_*,\bar y_N)$ is nonnegative and obeys this bound
with $(x,y)=(x_*,y_*)$. On bounded test sets the displayed upper bound is
$O(1/N)$. This is an ergodic gap statement; it is not a pointwise objective
bound and does not assert pointwise iterate convergence.

selected_current_proof_blocks: 1.1 Every exact proximal output lies in the effective domain of its function. Convexity therefore puts $\bar x_N$ in $\operatorname{dom}f$ and $\bar y_N$ in $\operatorname{dom}g^*$. [A1, F1, given, algebra]

proofparagraphs.text: By [F8], each low-frequency cosine difference in $L_j$ expands into the corresponding cosine/sine modes in $\mathcal T_N$. For even $N=2K$, its Nyquist term expands into $\cos(Kx)\cos(Kx_j)+\sin(Kx)\sin(Kx_j)$; [F7] makes the second coefficient zero because $Kx_j=\pi j$. At a grid difference $x_i-x_j=2\pi(i-j)/N$, Euler's identity [F6] rewrites the cosine sum defining $L_j(x_i)$ as the normalized sum of all characters in a complete residue system modulo $N$: for odd $N=2K+1$ the residues are $-K,\ldots,K$, and for even $N=2K$ they are $-K+1,\ldots,K$. Character orthogonality [F3] gives $L_j(x_i)=1$ when $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise. Thus $I_NU$ takes the prescribed nodal values and lies in $\mathcal T_N$. [F1, F3, F6, F7, F8, algebra]

proofparagraphs.text: By [F8], each low-frequency cosine difference in $L_j$ expands into the corresponding cosine/sine modes in $\mathcal T_N$. For even $N=2K$, its Nyquist term expands into $\cos(Kx)\cos(Kx_j)+\sin(Kx)\sin(Kx_j)$; [F7] makes the second coefficient zero because $Kx_j=\pi j$. At a grid difference $x_i-x_j=2\pi(i-j)/N$, Euler's identity [F6] rewrites the cosine sum defining $L_j(x_i)$ as the normalized sum of all characters in a complete residue system modulo $N$: for odd $N=2K+1$ the residues are $-K,\ldots,K$, and for even $N=2K$ they are $-K+1,\ldots,K$. Character orthogonality [F3] gives $L_j(x_i)=1$ when $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise. Thus $I_NU$ takes the prescribed nodal values and lies in $\mathcal T_N$. [F1, F3, F6, F7, F8, algebra]

The space $\mathcal T_N$ has exactly $N$ real basis modes. If two members agree at the $N$ nodes, their difference has zero nodal Fourier transform; inversion [F4] forces every frequency coefficient to vanish, so the interpolant is unique. [F1, F4, algebra]

Consider the augmented phase-fixed BVP of [[def-phase-bordered-periodic-orbit-bvp]] on $[0,1]$, with exact solution $u_*\in C^3$, field $\widetilde f$, and affine boundary map $B$. Put
$$M_2=\|u_*''\|_\infty,\quad M_3=\|u_*'''\|_\infty,\quad L_f=\sup\|D\widetilde f\|_2,\quad C_0=M_3/24+L_fM_2/8.$$
For every admitted mesh cell with midpoint $m_i$, assume the segment joining $u_*(m_i)$ to $(u_*(t_i)+u_*(t_{i+1}))/2$ lies in the field domain and $\|D\widetilde f\|_{\rm op}\le L_f$ on that segment. Let $G_h$ be the normalized midpoint residual on a uniform mesh and $Y^*$ the samples of $u_*$. Suppose that for all $0<h\le h_0$, $J_h=DG_h(Y^*)$ is invertible with $\|J_h^{-1}\|_{\infty\to\infty}\le K$, and on a fixed-radius ball of radius $r$ about $Y^*$ the maps $DG_h$ are $L_G$-Lipschitz in the block maximum norm. Assume $2KL_Gr\le1/2$, $KC_0h^2\le r/2$, and $2K^2L_GC_0h^2\le1/2$. Then $G_h$ has a unique zero $Y_h$ in that ball. Every candidate $Y$ in the ball satisfying $\|G_h(Y)\|_\infty\le\varepsilon$ obeys
$$
\|P_hY-u_*\|_\infty\le 4K\varepsilon+\left(2KC_0+\frac{M_2}{8}\right)h^2,
$$
where $P_h$ is linear interpolation of the node values. Thus the residual and discretization constants are explicit in the supplied derivative and inverse bounds. For the augmented state, the estimate includes both the orbit coordinates and the period coordinate.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Define concentrations $c_k(t)\ge0$ by the discrete product-kernel equations
$$\dot c_k=\frac12\sum_{i+j=k}ijc_ic_j-kc_k\sum_{j\ge1}jc_j,\qquad k\ge1,$$
with monomer initial data $c_1(0)=1$ and $c_k(0)=0$ for $k\ge2$. For $r=1,2$, define $M_r(t)=\sum_{k\ge1}k^rc_k(t)$. The pre-gelation solution is
$$c_k(t)=\frac{k^{k-2}}{k!}t^{k-1}e^{-kt},\qquad 0\le t<1,$$
where the value at $t=0$ is understood by continuity. Its first and second moments satisfy $M_1(t)=1$ and $M_2(t)=1/(1-t)$. Thus the second moment becomes unbounded at the finite time $t=1$ although the pre-gelation first moment is constant.

actualproofparagraphs.2.1: For every fixed $k$, differentiation of $a_kq^k/t$ gives $\dot c_k=c_k((k-1)/t-k)$. The gain coefficient in the $k$th product-kernel equation is $$\frac12\sum_{i+j=k}ijc_ic_j=\frac{q^k}{t^2}[z^k]\frac{T(z)^2}{2}=\frac{k-1}{t}c_k,$$ because $U=T-T^2/2$ implies $[z^k]T^2/2=(k-1)a_k$. The loss is $kc_kM_1=kc_k$ by step 1.1. Their difference is exactly $\dot c_k$, verifying every coefficient equation. As $t\downarrow0$, $c_1(t)\to1$ and $c_k(t)\to0$ for $k\ge2$, so the initial data hold. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

source_evidence.case_anchor: At k=1 the gain sum over positive i,j with i+j=k is empty, so its value is zero. Proof step 2.1 obtains the same zero from the coefficient (k-1)a_k; its limit gives the prescribed monomer initial data. The moment sums themselves have fixed index set k>=1.

proofparagraphs.text: Put $q(t)=te^{-t}$ and $a_k=k^{k-2}/k!$. For $0<t<1$, define $c_k(t)=a_kq(t)^k/t$. Since $q(t)<e^{-1}$, [F1] gives the convergent generating function $C(z,t)=\sum_{k\ge1}c_k(t)z^k=U(zq(t))/t$. Its mass generating function is $z\partial_zC=T(zq)/t$. Because $q=te^{-t}$ and $t\in[0,1)$, [F2] gives $T(q)=t$, so $M_1=z\partial_zC(1,t)=1$. [F1, F2, algebra]

additional_source_clauses.text:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, let $c:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be smooth (that is, $C^\infty$) with $1\le m<d$, let $M$ be a constant symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix, and let $V:U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. A **holonomic constraint** is the position condition $c(q)=0$. Write $J(q)=Dc(q)$, let $Q=\{q\in U:c(q)=0\}$, and define its regular part by $Q_{\mathrm{reg}}=\{q\in Q:\operatorname{rank}J(q)=m\}$. For $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A(q)=J(q)M^{-1}J(q)^T$ is positive definite. On a compact regular chart $K\subset Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A^{-1}$ is uniformly bounded: $\sup_{q\in K}\|A(q)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty$.

A position-momentum pair $(q,p)$ is **consistent** when $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$. The **regular constrained phase manifold** is
$$\mathcal M=\{(q,p)\in U\times\mathbb R^d:c(q)=0,\ J(q)M^{-1}p=0,\ q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}\}.$$
The ambient canonical two-form is $\omega_0=\sum_{i=1}^d dq_i\wedge dp_i$; its restriction to $\mathcal M$ is denoted $\omega_{\mathcal M}$.

For $v=M^{-1}p$, the constrained Hamilton equations are
$$\dot q=v,\qquad \dot p=-\nabla V(q)-J(q)^T\lambda,$$
with multiplier
$$\lambda=A(q)^{-1}\bigl(D^2c(q)[v,v]-J(q)M^{-1}\nabla V(q)\bigr).$$
Here $D^2c(q)[v,v]\in\mathbb R^m$ has components $v^TD^2c_j(q)v$. This multiplier is the one that keeps both $c(q)=0$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$ satisfied.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a compact subset of the regular phase manifold, contained in a convex phase-coordinate chart whose closure lies inside a regular chart. Let $(q,p)\in\mathcal C$, let $(q_1,p_1)$ be its exact RATTLE step, and let $(\widetilde q_1,\widetilde p_1)$ be a successful output of [[alg-finite-budget-rattle-step-with-scaled-residuals]] whose multiplier iterates remain in the chosen convex branch balls over $\mathcal C$. Define
$$\varepsilon_q=\|h^{-2}c(\widetilde q_1)\|_2,\qquad \varepsilon_p=\|h^{-1}J(\widetilde q_1)M^{-1}\widetilde p_1\|_2.$$
For sufficiently small $0<|h|$, there is a constant $C$ uniform over $\mathcal C$ such that
$$\|\widetilde q_1-q_1\|\le Ch^2\varepsilon_q,\qquad \|\widetilde p_1-p_1\|\le C|h|(\varepsilon_q+\varepsilon_p).$$
For the repeated-trajectory claim, choose compact phase tubes $\mathcal C_0\subset\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal C_1)$ in such a chart, with the coordinate image of $\mathcal C_1$ contained in a convex coordinate neighborhood with compact closure inside the regular chart. Suppose the exact-solve RATTLE iterates from a common initial state in $\mathcal C_0$ remain in $\mathcal C_0$ on the fixed-time grids under consideration. Restore each successful finite-solve output using a local retraction from [[lem-regular-holonomic-phase-residuals-control-distance-to-phase-manifold]] before using it as the next input. If both scaled residuals are bounded by a fixed sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ at each step, then for sufficiently small $h$ the restored trajectory remains in $\mathcal C_1$ and differs from the exact-solve RATTLE trajectory by $O(\varepsilon)$ uniformly on the grid. If instead both residuals are at most $C_0h^2$, the difference is $O(h^2)$, and the unscaled position and tangency residuals of each unprojected solver output are respectively $O(h^4)$ and $O(h^3)$. The finite solver's raw output need not be consistent, so the global estimate is for the restored trajectory.

proofparagraphs.text: The residual definitions give $\|c(\widetilde q_1)\|=|h|^2\varepsilon_q$ and $\|J(\widetilde q_1)M^{-1}\widetilde p_1\|=|h|\varepsilon_p$. Whenever the output lies in a neighborhood $U_j$ from [F6], its local retraction changes it by at most $C(|h|^2\varepsilon_q+|h|\varepsilon_p)\le C|h|(\varepsilon_q+\varepsilon_p)$ for $|h|\le1$. For the repeated-trajectory claim, choose a compact phase neighborhood $D$ of $\mathcal C_1$ with closure inside the regular chart. The compact branch bounds and $\Psi_0=\mathrm{id}$ imply $\Psi_h(\mathcal C_1)\subset D$ for sufficiently small $|h|$. Apply [F6] to $D$ and choose its finite retraction cover with a common distance constant. The union of these open domains contains the compact set $D$, hence contains some uniform ambient neighborhood of it. For every restored input in $\mathcal C_1$, step 3.1 puts its raw output within $O(|h|(\varepsilon_q+\varepsilon_p))$ of the exact step from that same input in $D$. Bounded scaled residuals and sufficiently small $|h|$ therefore place the raw output in this union. The same-input exact step need not belong to the reference tube $\mathcal C_0$. Thus the retraction is defined, and the restored update differs from the exact RATTLE update by at most $C|h|(\varepsilon_q+\varepsilon_p)$. [F1, F2, F3, F6, step 3.1, algebra]

The smooth momentum branch in [F2] changes that exact root by at most $C\varepsilon_q$ when $\widetilde\lambda$ replaces $\lambda$, using step 1.1 and the uniform branch derivative bound. additional_source_clauses.text:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, let $c:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be smooth (that is, $C^\infty$) with $1\le m<d$, let $M$ be a constant symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix, and let $V:U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. A **holonomic constraint** is the position condition $c(q)=0$. Write $J(q)=Dc(q)$, let $Q=\{q\in U:c(q)=0\}$, and define its regular part by $Q_{\mathrm{reg}}=\{q\in Q:\operatorname{rank}J(q)=m\}$. For $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A(q)=J(q)M^{-1}J(q)^T$ is positive definite. On a compact regular chart $K\subset Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A^{-1}$ is uniformly bounded: $\sup_{q\in K}\|A(q)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty$.

A position-momentum pair $(q,p)$ is **consistent** when $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$. The **regular constrained phase manifold** is
$$\mathcal M=\{(q,p)\in U\times\mathbb R^d:c(q)=0,\ J(q)M^{-1}p=0,\ q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}\}.$$
The ambient canonical two-form is $\omega_0=\sum_{i=1}^d dq_i\wedge dp_i$; its restriction to $\mathcal M$ is denoted $\omega_{\mathcal M}$.

For $v=M^{-1}p$, the constrained Hamilton equations are
$$\dot q=v,\qquad \dot p=-\nabla V(q)-J(q)^T\lambda,$$
with multiplier
$$\lambda=A(q)^{-1}\bigl(D^2c(q)[v,v]-J(q)M^{-1}\nabla V(q)\bigr).$$
Here $D^2c(q)[v,v]\in\mathbb R^m$ has components $v^TD^2c_j(q)v$. This multiplier is the one that keeps both $c(q)=0$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$ satisfied.

additional_source_clauses.text:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, let $c:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be smooth (that is, $C^\infty$) with $1\le m<d$, let $M$ be a constant symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix, and let $V:U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. A **holonomic constraint** is the position condition $c(q)=0$. Write $J(q)=Dc(q)$, let $Q=\{q\in U:c(q)=0\}$, and define its regular part by $Q_{\mathrm{reg}}=\{q\in Q:\operatorname{rank}J(q)=m\}$. For $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A(q)=J(q)M^{-1}J(q)^T$ is positive definite. On a compact regular chart $K\subset Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $A^{-1}$ is uniformly bounded: $\sup_{q\in K}\|A(q)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty$.

A position-momentum pair $(q,p)$ is **consistent** when $q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$. The **regular constrained phase manifold** is
$$\mathcal M=\{(q,p)\in U\times\mathbb R^d:c(q)=0,\ J(q)M^{-1}p=0,\ q\in Q_{\mathrm{reg}}\}.$$
The ambient canonical two-form is $\omega_0=\sum_{i=1}^d dq_i\wedge dp_i$; its restriction to $\mathcal M$ is denoted $\omega_{\mathcal M}$.

For $v=M^{-1}p$, the constrained Hamilton equations are
$$\dot q=v,\qquad \dot p=-\nabla V(q)-J(q)^T\lambda,$$
with multiplier
$$\lambda=A(q)^{-1}\bigl(D^2c(q)[v,v]-J(q)M^{-1}\nabla V(q)\bigr).$$
Here $D^2c(q)[v,v]\in\mathbb R^m$ has components $v^TD^2c_j(q)v$. This multiplier is the one that keeps both $c(q)=0$ and $J(q)M^{-1}p=0$ satisfied.

review_basis.full_actual_interface:
Let $f:D\to\mathbb R^d$ be $C^2$ on an open time-state domain, and let $y(t)$ be an exact solution on $[t_0,t_0+T]$. Fix $\gamma>0$ and a compact convex tube $Q\subset D$ containing the solution, all numerical states, and all state segments used below. Assume the bounds of [[lem-rosenbrock-euler-local-defect-and-residual-error]] hold uniformly on $Q$: $F,L,M_1$, an exact-J inverse bound $\kappa_0$, an approximate-J inverse bound $\kappa_1$, and $\|\widetilde J-D_yf\|_2\le\delta$. Assume $\|\widetilde J(t,u)-\widetilde J(t,v)\|_2\le L_J\|u-v\|_2$ on each state slice of $Q$, and $\|(I-\gamma h\widetilde J(t,y))^{-1}\|_2\le\kappa_1$ for all $0<h\le h_0$ and all relevant $(t,y)\in Q$. Fix the step size used below with $0<h\le h_0$.

At each step $t_n=t_0+nh$, use the one-stage algorithm of [[alg-rosenbrock-euler-step]] with a certified stage residual upper bound $\rho_n\le R h$, for a fixed $R\ge0$, and assume each call returns `success`, including its field evaluation, factorization, residual certification, and exact-storage checks. Starting from $y_0=y(t_0)$, suppose the computed states and comparison segments remain in $Q$ and $Nh\le T$. Then, with
$$C_E=\gamma\kappa_0LF+\frac{M_1}{2}+\gamma\kappa_0\kappa_1\delta F, \qquad C_s=\kappa_1L+\gamma\kappa_1^2L_JFh_0.$$
the global error obeys
$$
\|y_n-y(t_n)\|_2\le (C_E+\kappa_1R)T e^{C_sT}h\qquad(0\le n\le N).
$$
Thus the method is first order on this common tube when the linear solve residuals are $O(h)$. The theorem is conditional on the stated tube and inverse bounds; it does not prove that computed states stay in the tube.

For scalar stability, consider the exact-arithmetic complexification of the exact-Jacobian one-stage equation. For $\lambda,y,k\in\mathbb C$, $h>0$, $\gamma>0$, and $z=h\lambda$, use $(1-\gamma z)k=\lambda y$ and $y_+=y+hk$. Equivalently, identify $\mathbb C$ with $\mathbb R^2$ and multiplication by $\lambda$ with the real matrix $C_\lambda=\begin{pmatrix}\operatorname{Re}\lambda&-\operatorname{Im}\lambda\\\operatorname{Im}\lambda&\operatorname{Re}\lambda\end{pmatrix}$; the corresponding real exact Jacobian is $C_\lambda$, and the equations become $(I_2-\gamma h C_\lambda)k=C_\lambda y$ and $y_+=y+hk$. This is a scalar stability analysis of exact stage equations; it is not an execution of the finite-precision real algorithm [[alg-rosenbrock-euler-step]]. Use the scalar rational-function criteria in [[def-scalar-rk-a-and-l-stability]] for its amplification function. Its scalar stability function is
$$R_\gamma(z)=1+\frac{z}{1-\gamma z}=\frac{1+(1-\gamma)z}{1-\gamma z}.$$
It has no pole in $\operatorname{Re}z\le0$ and satisfies $|R_\gamma(z)|\le1$ throughout that half-plane if and only if $\gamma\ge\tfrac12$. Among these parameters, it is L-stable if and only if $\gamma=1$. In particular, the named Rosenbrock–Euler case $\gamma=1$ has the backward-Euler factor $R(z)=(1-z)^{-1}$.

review_basis.full_actual_interface:
Assume AC. Let $n,d\ge1$ and let $f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be convex, continuously differentiable, with $L$-Lipschitz gradients for a common $L>0$. Set $F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i$, assume $F$ is $\mu$-strongly convex for $\mu>0$, and let $x^*$ satisfy $\nabla F(x^*)=0$. Run [[alg-saga-finite-sum-method]] from deterministic $x_0$ with its standard initialized table and independent uniform component draws. For any constant $0<\eta\le1/(10L)$, define
$$V_k=\|x_k-x^*\|_2^2,\qquad S_k=\frac1n\sum_i\|\alpha_i^k-\nabla f_i(x^*)\|_2^2,\qquad \mathcal L_k=V_k+7\eta^2nS_k,$$
$$\delta=\min\{\mu\eta,1/(7n)\},\qquad q=1-\delta.$$
Then $0<\delta<1$, and for every $k\ge0$,
$$\mathbb E[\mathcal L_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\le q\mathcal L_k,\qquad \mathbb E[\mathcal L_k]\le q^k\mathcal L_0,\qquad \mathbb E[F(x_k)-F(x^*)]\le\frac L2q^k\mathcal L_0.$$
In particular $\eta=1/(10L)$ is allowed independently of $n$, with $\delta=\min\{\mu/(10L),1/(7n)\}$. When additionally $\mu\eta\le1/(7n)$ the factor is $1-\mu\eta$; no such faster factor is asserted without that condition. These are expectation bounds for the exact SAGA recurrence, not almost-sure convergence or finite-oracle success claims.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, $a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ bounded and coercive, and $F$ a bounded functional with the test-linearity required by $a$. Let $V_h$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space with norm $\|\cdot\|_h$, not necessarily a subspace of $V$. Suppose the algebraic sum $X_h=V+V_h$ is equipped with a norm extending these norms, and $\widetilde a_h:X_h\times V_h\to\mathbb K$ is a bounded extension of a discrete form $a_h$ with bound $M_h$. Assume $a_h$ is coercive on $V_h$ with constant $\alpha_h>0$, and let $F_h$ be bounded on $V_h$ with the matching test-linearity. The exact and discrete equations have unique solutions $u$ and $u_h$, and

$$\|u-u_h\|_h\le(1+M_h/\alpha_h)\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_h+\delta_h^{\mathrm{nc}}(u)/\alpha_h,$$

where $\delta_h^{\mathrm{nc}}(u)=\sup_{w_h\ne0}|F_h(w_h)-\widetilde a_h(u,w_h)|/\|w_h\|_h$. The estimate requires the bounded extension and does not assert that every nonconforming, penalty, or discontinuous Galerkin form has one.

For a family of these problems, suppose $M_h\le\overline M<\infty$ and $\alpha_h\ge\underline\alpha>0$ uniformly. Writing $E_h=\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_h$, the uniform bound is
$$\|u-u_h\|_h\le(1+\overline M/\underline\alpha)E_h+\delta_h^{\mathrm{nc}}(u)/\underline\alpha.$$
Thus uniform control of $E_h$ and $\delta_h^{\mathrm{nc}}(u)$ gives a uniform error budget; if both tend to zero, the errors tend to zero, and if both are $O(h^p)$ for a fixed $p>0$, the error is $O(h^p)$. No rate is inferred without those approximation, residual, and stability bounds.

actualproofparagraphs.2.1: Fix $v_h\in V_h$ and set $e_h:=u_h-v_h$. Then $e_h\in V_h$, and [A1] gives $\alpha_h\|e_h\|_h^2\le\operatorname{Re}a_h(e_h,e_h)=\operatorname{Re}(F_h(e_h)-\widetilde a_h(v_h,e_h))$. [A1, step 1.2, choose]
actualproofparagraphs.4.1: If $e_h=0$ there is nothing to divide by; otherwise divide step 3.1 by $\alpha_h\|e_h\|_h$. The triangle inequality gives $\|u-u_h\|_h\le(1+M_h/\alpha_h)\|u-v_h\|_h+\delta_h^{\mathrm{nc}}(u)/\alpha_h$. Taking the infimum over $v_h$ proves the per-mesh bound. For the stated family, replace $M_h/\alpha_h$ by $\overline M/\underline\alpha$ and $1/\alpha_h$ by $1/\underline\alpha$. The resulting constants are independent of $h$, yielding the stated uniform, convergence and rate consequences when the two explicit error terms have the corresponding control. [step 3.1, given, algebra] ∎

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Fix a finite pivot grid with $m$ retained bins, endpoint $R$, final time $T$, mesh $h=T/N$, and the initial projection/reservoir convention of [[thm-sectional-semiflow-cutoff-error-budget]]. Let $y^k$ be the successful forward-Euler states under the uniform positivity CFL, and let $\nu_t^R$ be the exact finite-sectional retained measure. There are constants $C_{E,T,R,\Delta}$ and $C_T$ independent of $N$ such that
$$d_{BL}\left(\sum_i n_i^N\delta_{x_i},\mu_T\right)\le \sqrt m\,C_{E,T,R,\Delta}h+e^{C_TT}\left[C_QT\Delta+\frac\Delta2M_0(\mu_T)+\frac{M_1}R+\frac{2K_*M_1^2T}{aR}\right].$$
The first term is temporal error for the fixed finite ODE; the terms in $\Delta$ and $R^{-1}$ are the separate grid and cutoff errors. The temporal constant may depend on the fixed grid and cutoff.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $d\ge1$, let $f:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and use a level
hierarchy as in [[def-smolyak-univariate-level-hierarchy]]. Suppose its tensor
rules satisfy $Q_L^{\otimes d}(f)\to I_d(f)$ and its detail family is absolutely
summable in the sense of [[def-smolyak-absolute-detail-summability]]. For every
finite downward-closed $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb N_0^d$ containing $0$,
$$|I_d(f)-Q_\Lambda(f)|\le\sum_{\ell\in\mathbb N_0^d\setminus\Lambda}|\delta_\ell(f)|.$$
In particular, the dyadic composite-Simpson hierarchy satisfies the convergence
hypothesis for continuous $f$ by
[[lem-smolyak-dyadic-tensor-simpson-convergence]], and for the mixed-derivative
class of [[lem-smolyak-mixed-simpson-detail-decay]] the same hierarchy also
satisfies absolute summability.

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: Choose $L$ large enough that $\Lambda\subseteq R_L$. By [F1], [F3], and [F6], $Q_L^{\otimes d}(f)-Q_\Lambda(f)=\sum_{\ell\in R_L\setminus\Lambda}\delta_\ell(f)$. The index set on the right is finite and is contained in $\mathbb N_0^d\setminus\Lambda$. [given, F1, F3, F6, choose]
actualproofparagraphs.2.1: By [F5] and [F2], the absolute value of the right side in step 1.1 is at most the omitted-detail tail $T_\Lambda:=\sum_{\ell\notin\Lambda}|\delta_\ell(f)|$ for every sufficiently large $L$. Put $x_L:=Q_L^{\otimes d}(f)-Q_\Lambda(f)$ and $z:=I_d(f)-Q_\Lambda(f)$; the convergence hypothesis in **Given** says $|x_L-z|=|Q_L^{\otimes d}(f)-I_d(f)|$ is eventually below every positive rational tolerance. If $|z|>T_\Lambda$, [F10] supplies a positive rational $\varepsilon$ with $2\varepsilon<|z|-T_\Lambda$. For sufficiently large $L$, both $\Lambda\subseteq R_L$ and $|x_L-z|<\varepsilon$ hold by finiteness of $\Lambda$ and [F7]. The triangle inequality [F8] then gives $|x_L|\ge |z|-|x_L-z|>|z|-\varepsilon>T_\Lambda$, contradicting the preceding tail bound. Hence the displayed omitted-tail inequality holds. [given, F2, F5, F7, F8, F10, step 1.1, algebra]

source_evidence.case_anchor: Lambda contains zero, but R_L minus Lambda in proof step 1.1 can be empty; its finite sum is then zero. Proof step 2.1 bounds that value by the nonnegative omitted-detail tail, which also may be zero. The reconstruction limit and tail argument never require a nonzero omitted detail.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Use the dyadic composite-Simpson hierarchy of
[[def-smolyak-univariate-level-hierarchy]]. Let $d\ge1$, $n\ge2d$, and let
$f:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb R$ satisfy the
continuous mixed fourth-derivative hypotheses and bounds $M_S$ of
[[lem-smolyak-mixed-simpson-detail-decay]]. Define the isotropic index set
$$\Lambda_n:=\{\ell\in\mathbb N_0^d:|\ell|_1\le n\},$$
and let $W_{n,d}:=|\mathcal N_{\Lambda_n}|$ be the distinct-node work count
of [[def-smolyak-cubature]] and [[alg-smolyak-node-deduplication]]. For a
dyadic node $x$, let $t(x)=0$ for $x=0,1,1/2$; if $x=p/2^{r+1}$ is interior
and reduced with odd numerator $p$, let $t(x)=r\ge1$. Put
$$a_0:=3,\qquad a_r:=2^r\ (r\ge1),$$
$$\|f\|_{\mathrm{mix},d}:=\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}}\left(\frac{17}{2880}\right)^{|S|}M_S,\quad T_d:=\sup_{N\ge1}\sum_{r=1}^{N}r^{d-1}16^{-r},$$
$$D_d:=2\cdot3^d d^{d-1},\qquad C_d:=D_d^4T_d\left(\frac3{\log 2}\right)^{5(d-1)},$$
where $\log$ is the natural logarithm of [[def-natural-logarithm]]. Then
$T_d<\infty$, and the actual node-union count and error satisfy
$$W_{n,d}=\sum_{\substack{t\in\mathbb N_0^d\\|t|_1\le n}}\prod_{j=1}^d a_{t_j},\qquad 2^n\binom{n-1}{d-1}\le W_{n,d}\le D_d2^n(n+1)^{d-1},$$

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $x_*$ be a KKT point of a $C^2$ program with active inequality set
$I=I(x_*)$, multiplier $\mu_*=(\nu_*,\lambda_{*,I})$, and active
constraint vector $c=(h,g_I)$. Assume LICQ, strict complementarity
$\lambda_{*,i}>0$ for $i\in I$, and the second-order sufficient condition
$d^TH_*d>0$ for every nonzero $d\in\ker A_*$, where
$A_*=Dc(x_*)$ and $H_*=\nabla^2_{xx}L(x_*,\mu_*)$.

For all sufficiently large fixed $\rho$, the PHR augmented-Lagrangian
multiplier update has a local contraction when each inner minimization is
solved exactly. When $r>0$, the same local multiplier convergence holds for inner
points $\widehat x_k$ with stationarity residuals
$\epsilon_k=\|\nabla_x\mathcal L_\rho(\widehat x_k,\nu_k,\lambda_k)\|_2$
whose sum is sufficiently small, provided each point stays in the local
strongly convex branch. More precisely, there are local radii $\delta_\mu$
and $d_x>0$, a strong-convexity constant $\alpha>0$, and a contraction
factor $q<1$ such that convergence holds whenever
$$\|\mu_0-\mu_*\|_2\le\delta_\mu/2,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^\infty\epsilon_k\le \min\left\{\alpha d_x,\frac{(1-q)\delta_\mu}{2C}\right\},$$
where $C=\rho L_c/\alpha$ and $L_c$ is a Lipschitz constant for $c$ on
the local primal neighborhood. Inactive multipliers are initialized at
zero. If $c$ has zero components, the multiplier update is absent and the
bound involving $C$ is omitted; sufficiently local inner points with
summable residuals converge to $x_*$ by strong convexity.

This is a limit theorem for an infinite sequence of successful inner
returns. The contraction estimates apply to any successful prefix of the
finite-budget procedure; the limit conclusion applies only to an infinite
continuation whose calls continue to return within their finite inner caps.
For that procedure, the residual sequence in this theorem is the reported
$\widehat\epsilon_k$; its input tolerances must be chosen so these reports
satisfy the displayed summability bound.

Let $x_*$ be a KKT point of a $C^2$ program with active inequality set
$I=I(x_*)$, multiplier $\mu_*=(\nu_*,\lambda_{*,I})$, and active
constraint vector $c=(h,g_I)$. Assume LICQ, strict complementarity
$\lambda_{*,i}>0$ for $i\in I$, and the second-order sufficient condition
$d^TH_*d>0$ for every nonzero $d\in\ker A_*$, where
$A_*=Dc(x_*)$ and $H_*=\nabla^2_{xx}L(x_*,\mu_*)$.

proofparagraphs.text: Write $A=A_*$, $H=H_*$ and $r=\dim c$. Strict complementarity and continuity give a neighborhood in which every active inequality satisfies $\lambda_i+\rho g_i(x)>0$ and every inactive inequality, whose multiplier is initialized at zero, satisfies $\lambda_j+\rho g_j(x)<0$. On this branch, [F2] reduces the $x$-dependent augmented Lagrangian to $$\Phi_\rho(x,\mu)=f(x)+\mu^Tc(x)+\frac\rho2\|c(x)\|_2^2,$$ where $\mu=(\nu,\lambda_I)$. Its gradient vanishes at $(x_*,\mu_*)$. [given, F1, F2, algebra, algebra]

The $x$-Hessian at the base point is $W_\rho=H+\rho A^TA$. If $r=0$, the assumed condition says $H\succ0$. For $r>0$, choose orthonormal matrices $Z,Y$ spanning $\ker A$ and its orthogonal complement, respectively; then $C_0=AY$ is invertible. In this basis the tangent block is $H_T=Z^THZ\succ0$ when its dimension is positive, the cross blocks are those of $H$, and the normal block is $Y^THY+\rho C_0^TC_0$. Its Schur complement over the tangent block is $D+\rho C_0^TC_0$, where $D=Y^THY-Y^THZ H_T^{-1}Z^THY$; if the tangent block is empty, take $D=Y^THY$. Since $C_0^TC_0\succ0$, this Schur complement is positive definite for sufficiently large $\rho$. Hence $W_\rho\succ0$. [given, algebra, choose]

actualproofparagraphs.3.1: For $r>0$, the exact multiplier map is $T(\mu)=\mu+\rho c(x(\mu))$, so $$DT(\mu_*)=I-\rho A W_\rho^{-1}A^T.$$ In the orthonormal coordinates of step 1.2, block elimination gives $A W_\rho^{-1}A^T=C_0(D+\rho C_0^TC_0)^{-1}C_0^T$ $=(\rho I+E)^{-1}$, where $E=C_0^{-T}DC_0^{-1}$ is symmetric. Continuity of $DT$ then gives a closed multiplier ball on which $T$ is a contraction with some factor $q<1$. For $r=0$ the multiplier update is absent. [step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

For the sum, any fixed finite prefix tends to zero as $k\to\infty$, while the remaining tail is bounded by $C\sum_{j\ge J}\epsilon_j$, which tends to zero as $J\to\infty$. Therefore $\mu_k\to\mu_*$. Also $\epsilon_k\to0$ because it is summable, so step 4.1 gives $\widehat x_k-x(\mu_k)\to0$ and continuity gives $\widehat x_k\to x_*$. When $r=0$, step 1.2 gives a strongly convex local objective and the same residual estimate directly yields $\widehat x_k\to x_*$. [given, A1, A2, step 4.1, algebra]

source_evidence.case_anchor: Proof step 5.1 starts the residual convolution at k=0, where the sum over 0<=j<k is empty and equals zero. The Statement separately omits the multiplier restriction when r=0; proof steps 1.2, 2.1 and 3.1 treat that zero-dimensional active system. The infinite residual sum itself is indexed by all nonnegative integers.

$d^TH_*d>0$ for every nonzero $d\in\ker A_*$, where
$A_*=Dc(x_*)$ and $H_*=\nabla^2_{xx}L(x_*,\mu_*)$.

multiplier update has a local contraction when each inner minimization is
solved exactly. When $r>0$, the same local multiplier convergence holds for inner
points $\widehat x_k$ with stationarity residuals

strongly convex branch. More precisely, there are local radii $\delta_\mu$

summable residuals converge to $x_*$ by strong convexity.

proofparagraphs.text: Write $A=A_*$, $H=H_*$ and $r=\dim c$. On this branch, [F2] reduces the $x$-dependent augmented Lagrangian to $$\Phi_\rho(x,\mu)=f(x)+\mu^Tc(x)+\frac\rho2\|c(x)\|_2^2,$$ where $\mu=(\nu,\lambda_I)$. Its gradient vanishes at $(x_*,\mu_*)$. The $x$-Hessian at the base point is $W_\rho=H+\rho A^TA$. If $r=0$, the assumed condition says $H\succ0$. source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $F_A$ be the active KKT map defined in
[[alg-sqp-exact-hessian-newton-step]]. Let the program be $C^2$, with a
correct locally identified active set,
LICQ, strict complementarity, and the second-order sufficient condition.
Assume the active KKT map $F_A$ has a locally Lipschitz Jacobian near the
solution. At each nonterminal iterate let $P_k$ project onto
$\ker A_k$, where $A_k=Dc_A(x_k)$ is the Jacobian of the identified
active constraints. Set $z_k=(x_k,\mu_k)$,
$F_k=F_A(z_k)$, $J_k=DF_A(z_k)$, and
$s_k=(p_k,\delta\mu_k)$ for the computed reduced-BFGS step. Let $H_k$ be
the exact Lagrangian Hessian and $B_k$ the symmetric positive-definite
model. Suppose the reduced-BFGS KKT matrices
$\widetilde J_k$ are nonsingular with
$\sup_k\|\widetilde J_k^{-1}\|_2<\infty$, and the reduced Dennis–Moré
condition holds along the computed primal steps $p_k$:
$$\frac{\|P_k(B_k-H_k)P_kp_k\|_2}{\|p_k\|_2}\longrightarrow0 \quad\text{whenever }p_k\ne0.$$
Also assume the exact Newton residual ratios satisfy
$\|J_ks_k+F_k\|_2\le\bar\eta\|F_k\|_2$ for every nonterminal $k$, for
some fixed $\bar\eta<1$.
Then full steps of [[alg-sqp-reduced-bfgs-kkt-step]] started sufficiently
near the KKT pair converge superlinearly, unless an exact root is reached
first. No globalization or global BFGS convergence claim is made.

The Dennis–Moré condition supplies numbers $\delta_k\to0$ with $\|r_k\|_2\le\delta_k\|p_k\|_2$ whenever $p_k\ne0$; therefore $\|r_k\|_2\le C\delta_k\|F_k\|_2$. At a zero primal step the displayed residual is zero, so the same conclusion holds. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

Let $c_A:U\to\mathbb R^r$ with $r\ge1$ be $C^2$ on a convex ball about $x$, and assume
$\|D^2c_A(z)[u,v]\|_2\le M\|u\|_2\|v\|_2$ throughout that ball. Let
$A=Dc_A(x)$ have smallest singular value at least $s_0>0$, and let $p$ be
small enough that $x+p$ and the correction segment stay in the ball. If
$c_A(x)+Ap=0$ and $w$ is the correction of
[[alg-sqp-second-order-correction]], then
$$\|w\|_2\le\frac{M}{2s_0}\|p\|_2^2, \qquad \|c_A(x+p+w)\|_2=O(\|p\|_2^3)\quad(p\to0).$$
The correction is the unique minimum-norm vector satisfying
$Aw=-c_A(x+p)$.

Consider a feasible SQP quadratic subproblem with $B\succ0$, $m$ inequality
rows, and $r$ independent equality rows. Run
[[alg-sqp-feasible-working-set-qp-solve]] with an independent initial working
set and cap $N\ge(n+2)2^m$. Assume exact subproblem solves, every nonzero
working-set direction has a strictly positive maximal feasible step, and a
blocker is selected by the algorithm's least-index tie rule. Then the
algorithm returns the unique global minimizer and a KKT certificate in at
most $N$ iterations. If a zero blocking step, dependent blocker, failed solve,
or smaller user cap occurs, the algorithm returns its stated inconclusive
status and no optimality claim follows.

The positive-step hypothesis is the nondegeneracy condition that prevents
zero-length working-set cycling. The proof also shows that a working set
already minimized with negative multipliers cannot recur after progress.

proofparagraphs.text: Let $z$ be a feasible iterate, $W$ its working set, and $u\ne0$ the exact direction minimizer. Its KKT equation is $Bu+(Bz+c)+A^T\nu+\sum_{i\in W}\mu_iG_i^T=0$, with $Au=0$ and $G_iu=0$ for $i\in W$. Multiplying by $u^T$ gives $(Bz+c)^Tu=-u^TBu$. Hence for every accepted $0<\alpha\le1$, $$q(z+\alpha u)-q(z)=-\alpha(1-\alpha/2)u^TBu<0.$$ If $\alpha<1$, a blocking row cannot lie in the span of the current rows, since it has $G_iu>0$ while every row in that span annihilates $u$; adding it preserves independence. [A1, F1, F2, algebra]

Suppose instead $u=0$ and the multiplier of a working inequality $j$ is negative. After deleting $j$, let $v$ be the next exact direction. The new direction stationarity, dotted with $v$, gives $(Bz+c)^Tv=-v^TBv$. The old face stationarity, also dotted with $v$, gives $(Bz+c)^Tv+\mu_jG_jv=0$, because all retained working rows annihilate $v$. Therefore $\mu_jG_jv=v^TBv>0$, so $v\ne0$ and $G_jv<0$. The dropped inequality is feasible to first order, and by the positive-step hypothesis the next iterate moves strictly along this descent direction. [A1, F1, F2, algebra]

Assume AC. Let $d,m\ge1$ be finite, $T>0$, and let $W$ and $\xi$ satisfy
the filtered Brownian hypotheses in
[[def-locally-lipschitz-ito-sde-and-maximal-solution]] with $U=\mathbb R^d$.
Consider the autonomous SDE
$$dX_t=b(X_t)\,dt+\sigma(X_t)\,dW_t,\qquad X_0=\xi,$$
where $b\in C^1(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)$, $\sigma:\mathbb R^d\to
\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ is globally Lipschitz, and for constants $L,C<\infty$
and an integer $q\ge1$,
$$\langle x-y,b(x)-b(y)\rangle\le L|x-y|^2, \qquad \|Db(x)\|\le C(1+|x|^q).$$
Suppose $\mathbb E|\xi|^p<\infty$ for every finite $p\ge1$. Then the
maximal local strong solution is global on $[0,T]$, is unique up to
indistinguishability, and for every finite $p\ge1$,
$$\mathbb E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t|^p<\infty.$$
The bound may depend on $p,T$, the coefficient constants, and the initial
moments. No global Lipschitz condition on the drift is assumed.

review_basis.full_actual_interface:
Let $n,d\ge1$, and let $f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be convex, continuously differentiable, with $L$-Lipschitz gradients for a common $L>0$. Put $F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i$, assume $F$ is $\mu$-strongly convex for $\mu>0$, and let $x^*$ satisfy $\nabla F(x^*)=0$. In one SVRG epoch [[alg-svrg-finite-sum-method]], take a deterministic snapshot $\widetilde x$, set $x_0=\widetilde x$, choose

$$\eta=\frac1{10L},\qquad m=2n,$$

and choose each uniform inner index independently of the past. Assume $n\ge10L/\mu$. Choose the output index $J$ independently and uniformly from $\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$. Then

$$\mathbb E[F(x_J)-F(x^*)]\le q\bigl(F(\widetilde x)-F(x^*)\bigr),\qquad q=\frac{1}{\mu\eta(1-2L\eta)m}+\frac{2L\eta}{1-2L\eta}\le\frac78.$$

The expectation is over the inner indices and $J$; this is an epoch expectation bound and asserts no almost-sure convergence.
review_basis.source_specific_focus: The chosen step one over ten L and epoch length twice n bound the independently sampled output objective gap by the explicit factor at most seven eighths.

review_basis.full_actual_interface:
For every nonstationary trial of [[alg-trust-region-method]], the selected
predicted reduction is positive, and every accepted trial strictly decreases
the objective.

Assume the hypotheses and parameter ranges of
[[thm-trust-region-global-liminf-gradient]], and let $f_{inf}$ be a lower
bound for $f$. For each target $0<\varepsilon\le1$, run
[[alg-trust-region-method]] until its first iterate with
$\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2\le\varepsilon$. Define
$$c_\delta:=\min\left\{\frac1{2M_B}, \frac{\theta_C(1-\eta_2)}{2(L+M_B)}\right\},\qquad c_R:=\min\{\Delta_0,\gamma_{dec}\min\{c_\delta,\Delta_{max}\}\},$$
where a zero denominator means $+\infty$, and put
$$c_P:=\min\{c_R,1/M_B\},\qquad c_S:=\tfrac12\eta_1\theta_Cc_P>0.$$
Then the number $N_s$ of accepted steps before reaching the target and the
number $N_u$ of rejected trials obey
$$N_s\le\frac{f(x_0)-f_{inf}}{c_S\varepsilon^2},$$
$$N_u\le\frac{\log(\Delta_0/r_\varepsilon)+N_s\log\gamma_{inc}} {|\log\gamma_{dec}|},\qquad r_\varepsilon:=\min\{\Delta_0,\gamma_{dec}\min\{c_\delta\varepsilon, \Delta_{max}\}\}.$$
Here $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm of a positive real.
Consequently, accepted steps and total trials $N_s+N_u$ are
$O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. An outer cap at least
the resulting total-trial bound suffices for the finite-budget algorithm to
return `target-achieved` or `stationary`, with gradient norm at most
$\varepsilon$.

review_basis.full_actual_interface:
Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, bounded below, and have an
$L$-Lipschitz gradient on every trial segment. At every iteration let $B_k$
be symmetric with $\|B_k\|_2\le M_B$ for a fixed $M_B\ge0$. Run an infinite
trust-region process of [[alg-trust-region-method]] with no positive target
and no outer cap, fixed $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$,
$0<\gamma_{dec}<1<\gamma_{inc}$, $0<\theta_C\le1$, and
$0<\Delta_0\le\Delta_{max}$. If it does not terminate at a stationary
point, then
$$\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2=0.$$

source_evidence.full_current_interface:
Use the equality-constrained problem and exact recurrence of
[[alg-two-block-admm-scaled]]. Suppose $f,g$ are proper closed convex, a
Lagrangian saddle point $(x_*,z_*,y_*)$ exists, $\rho>0$, and every outer
subproblem is attained exactly. Write $p_*=f(x_*)+g(z_*)$. Then
$$r^k\to0,\qquad f(x^k)+g(z^k)\to p_*,\qquad y^k\to\bar y$$
for some dual optimum $\bar y$ of
$d(y)=\inf_{x,z}\mathcal L((x,z),y)$. The theorem does not assert convergence
of $x^k$ or $z^k$.
source_evidence.item_specific_mathematical_focus: A saddle point and exactly attained block sweeps yield primal residual, objective and dual convergence; individual primal-block iterates are not claimed convergent.
selected_current_proof_blocks: 2.1 Fixing $z=z_*$ and then $x=x_*$ in the right saddle inequality gives $-K^*y_*\in\partial f(x_*)$ and $-L^*y_*\in\partial g(z_*)$. By [F6], $f(x_*)+f^*(-K^*y_*)=-\langle y_*,Kx_*\rangle,\qquad g(z_*)+g^*(-L^*y_*)=-\langle y_*,Lz_*\rangle.$ Each component infimum is below a finite value because $f,g$ are proper, so neither equals $+\infty$. If both are finite, choosing independent points within any $\epsilon>0$ of them proves that the joint infimum is their sum; if either is $-\infty$, fixing a finite competitor in the other block and sending the first block value down shows the joint infimum is $-\infty$. Thus separating the $x$ and $z$ infima and using [F4] gives the extended-real identity $$d(y)=-f^*(-K^*y)-g^*(-L^*y)-\langle y,c\rangle.$$ The terms are well-defined because [F5] excludes $-\infty$ conjugate values. Substituting the two equalities and feasibility into the formula gives $d(y_*)=p_*$. The dual solution set $Y_*:=\{y:d(y)=p_*\}$ is nonempty. Weak duality gives $d(y)\le p_*$, so $y\in Y_*$ iff $\mathcal L((x,z),y)\ge p_*$ for every $x,z$. Each finite-valued pair $(x,z)$ imposes a closed affine half-space in $y$; an infinite-valued pair imposes no restriction. Thus $Y_*$ is closed and convex as an intersection of closed convex sets. [A1, F1, F2, F4, F5, F6, step 1.1, algebra, algebra]

selected_current_proof_blocks: 1.1 The left saddle inequality forces $Kx_*+Lz_*=c$: otherwise taking $y=y_*+t(Kx_*+Lz_*-c)$ and letting $t\to+\infty$ contradicts its finite upper bound. For every $y$, the dual value $d(y)$ is at most $\mathcal L((x_*,z_*),y)=p_*$. At $y_*$, the right saddle inequality gives $d(y_*)\ge p_*$; hence $d(y_*)=p_*$ and $y_*$ is dual optimal. [A1, F1, F3, F8, algebra]

Let $f:D\to\mathbb R^d$ be $C^2$ on an open time-state domain and let $y(t)$ solve $y'=f(t,y)$ on $[t_0,t_0+T]$. Fix $\alpha=1-1/\sqrt2$, $h_0>0$, and a compact convex tube $Q\subset D$ containing the exact and computed states, all stage midpoint segments, and the line segments between states compared below. Use a fixed step size satisfying $0<h\le h_0$. Assume on $Q$ that
$$
\|f\|_2\le F,\quad\|D_yf\|_2\le L,\quad\|f_t\|_2\le T_0,\quad\|D^2f\|_{\rm op}\le H,
$$
and that $\|\widetilde J(t,y)\|_2\le B_J$, $\|\widetilde T(t,y)\|_2\le B_T$, with state-Lipschitz bounds $\|\widetilde J(t,u)-\widetilde J(t,v)\|_2\le L_J\|u-v\|_2$ and $\|\widetilde T(t,u)-\widetilde T(t,v)\|_2\le L_T\|u-v\|_2$. Suppose $\|\alpha h\widetilde J(t,y)\|_2\le q<1$ for all $0<h\le h_0$ and relevant $(t,y)$; put $\kappa=(1-q)^{-1}$. Define the constants $C_1,K_1,C_F,C_K,M_2,C_r$ from [[lem-two-stage-rosenbrock-local-defect-and-residual-error]] using $h_0$ in $K_1=F+\alpha h_0\kappa C_1$, and put $C_{loc}=C_K+M_2/6$.

Use the method of [[alg-two-stage-rosenbrock-w-method]] with stage residual upper bounds $\rho_{1,n}\le R_1h$ and $\rho_{2,n}\le R_2h^2$, where $R_1,R_2$ are fixed, and assume each call returns `success`, including both field evaluations, residual certifications, and exact-storage checks. Starting from $y_0=y(t_0)$ and assuming $Nh\le T$ and all stated tube conditions hold, define
$$
G_1=F+\alpha h_0B_T,\quad K_s=\kappa G_1,
$$
$$
L_1=\kappa(L+\alpha h_0L_T)+\alpha h_0\kappa^2L_JG_1,
$$
$$
V=F+\alpha h_0B_JK_s,
$$
$$L_V=L(1+h_0L_1/2)+\alpha h_0(L_JK_s+B_JL_1),\qquad L_2=\kappa L_V+\alpha h_0\kappa^2L_JV.$$
Then the global error satisfies
$$
\|y_n-y(t_n)\|_2\le(C_{loc}+C_rR_1+\kappa R_2)T e^{L_2T}h^2\qquad(0\le n\le N).
$$
This is a conditional order-two theorem on the common tube. Its constants and assumptions permit both the exact-J branch and the bounded W-method branch; scalar A/L-stability is asserted separately only for the exact-J branch.

review_basis.full_actual_interface:
Let $f:D\to\mathbb R^d$ be $C^2$ on an open time-state domain and let $y(t)$ solve $y'=f(t,y)$ on $[t_0,t_0+T]$. Fix $\alpha=1-1/\sqrt2$, $h_0>0$, and a compact convex tube $Q\subset D$ containing the exact and computed states, all stage midpoint segments, and the line segments between states compared below. Use a fixed step size satisfying $0<h\le h_0$. Assume on $Q$ that
$$
\|f\|_2\le F,\quad\|D_yf\|_2\le L,\quad\|f_t\|_2\le T_0,\quad\|D^2f\|_{\rm op}\le H,
$$
and that $\|\widetilde J(t,y)\|_2\le B_J$, $\|\widetilde T(t,y)\|_2\le B_T$, with state-Lipschitz bounds $\|\widetilde J(t,u)-\widetilde J(t,v)\|_2\le L_J\|u-v\|_2$ and $\|\widetilde T(t,u)-\widetilde T(t,v)\|_2\le L_T\|u-v\|_2$. Suppose $\|\alpha h\widetilde J(t,y)\|_2\le q<1$ for all $0<h\le h_0$ and relevant $(t,y)$; put $\kappa=(1-q)^{-1}$. Define the constants $C_1,K_1,C_F,C_K,M_2,C_r$ from [[lem-two-stage-rosenbrock-local-defect-and-residual-error]] using $h_0$ in $K_1=F+\alpha h_0\kappa C_1$, and put $C_{loc}=C_K+M_2/6$.

Use the method of [[alg-two-stage-rosenbrock-w-method]] with stage residual upper bounds $\rho_{1,n}\le R_1h$ and $\rho_{2,n}\le R_2h^2$, where $R_1,R_2$ are fixed, and assume each call returns `success`, including both field evaluations, residual certifications, and exact-storage checks. Starting from $y_0=y(t_0)$ and assuming $Nh\le T$ and all stated tube conditions hold, define
$$
G_1=F+\alpha h_0B_T,\quad K_s=\kappa G_1,
$$
$$
L_1=\kappa(L+\alpha h_0L_T)+\alpha h_0\kappa^2L_JG_1,
$$
$$
V=F+\alpha h_0B_JK_s,
$$
$$L_V=L(1+h_0L_1/2)+\alpha h_0(L_JK_s+B_JL_1),\qquad L_2=\kappa L_V+\alpha h_0\kappa^2L_JV.$$
Then the global error satisfies
$$
\|y_n-y(t_n)\|_2\le(C_{loc}+C_rR_1+\kappa R_2)T e^{L_2T}h^2\qquad(0\le n\le N).
$$
This is a conditional order-two theorem on the common tube. Its constants and assumptions permit both the exact-J branch and the bounded W-method branch; scalar A/L-stability is asserted separately only for the exact-J branch.

review_basis.full_actual_interface:
For scalar stability, consider the exact-arithmetic complexification of the exact-Jacobian stage equations of [[alg-two-stage-rosenbrock-w-method]]. For $\lambda,y,k_1,q_2,k_2\in\mathbb C$, $h>0$, $z=h\lambda$, and $\alpha=1-1/\sqrt2$, use
$$
(1-\alpha z)k_1=\lambda y,\qquad F_1=\lambda(y+hk_1/2),\qquad (1-\alpha z)q_2=F_1-k_1,\qquad k_2=q_2+k_1,\qquad y_+=y+hk_2.
$$
Equivalently, identify $\mathbb C$ with $\mathbb R^2$ and multiplication by $\lambda$ with $C_\lambda=\begin{pmatrix}\operatorname{Re}\lambda&-\operatorname{Im}\lambda\\\operatorname{Im}\lambda&\operatorname{Re}\lambda\end{pmatrix}$ in the real stage equations, with exact-J data $\widetilde J=C_\lambda$ and $\widetilde T=0$. This is a scalar stability analysis of exact stage equations; it is not an execution of the finite-precision real algorithm. Use the scalar rational-function criteria in [[def-scalar-rk-a-and-l-stability]] for its amplification function. Its scalar stability function is
$$R(z)=\frac{1+(1-2\alpha)z}{(1-\alpha z)^2}.$$
This function has no pole on $\operatorname{Re}z\le0$, has modulus at most one there, and tends to zero as $|z|\to\infty$ in that half-plane. Hence this exact-J scalar method is L-stable. This theorem makes no A/L-stability claim for an arbitrary approximate Jacobian.
review_basis.source_specific_focus: The exact-J corrected scalar rational amplification has no left-half-plane pole, bounded modulus and vanishing stiff limit; arbitrary W approximations receive no such guarantee.

Every choice of $A,b$ was arbitrary, proving the uniform conclusion. [given, F1, F2, F4, step 1.1] ∎

If that procedure returns success with boxes $Q_0,\ldots,Q_{N-1}$ and $Y_N$, then for every $(x_0,\theta)\in X_0\times\Theta$ the unique solution of $y'=H(y)$ from $(x_0,I_d,\theta)$ exists through time $1$, its trajectory on $[n/N,(n+1)/N]$ lies in $Q_n$, and its terminal state lies in $Y_N$. Consequently the endpoint state encloses $\phi_\theta(x_0)$ and the matrix block encloses $D_x\phi_\theta(x_0)$.
source_evidence.item_specific_mathematical_focus: A successful verified range-provider Euler enclosure contains every admitted scaled trajectory and terminal monodromy block through the unit interval.
selected_current_proof_blocks: 1.1 Fix any exact state $y_n\in Y_n$ at time $nh$. While its solution remains in $K$, [F1] gives $\|H(y(t))\|_\infty\le M$, hence $\|y(t)-y_n\|_\infty\le M(t-nh)\le Mh$. If it first left $K$ before $nh+h$, continuity would place the exit point in $Q_n\subseteq K$, a contradiction. Thus the solution exists throughout this cell and stays in $Q_n$. [F1, F2, F3, given]

4.1 For $H(x,Z,\theta)=(\theta f(x),\theta Df(x)Z,0)$, the state block solves $x'=\theta f(x)$ and the matrix block solves $Z'=\theta Df(x)Z$ with $Z(0)=I_d$. Rescaling physical time $t=\theta s$ makes the state block $\phi_{\theta s}(x_0)$; [F4] identifies $Z(s)$ with its derivative in $x_0$. The terminal block inclusions from step 3.1 are therefore the claimed flow and monodromy enclosures. [F2, F4, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Under the hypotheses of [[def-weighted-orthogonal-polynomial-galerkin-space]], for every real measurable $u$ such that $\int|u p_j|\,d\mu<\infty$ for $0\le j\le N$, the formula
$$
\Pi_Nu=\sum_{j=0}^{N}\frac{\int u(x)p_j(x)\,d\mu(x)}{h_j}\,p_j
$$
is finite and defines the unique element of $V_N(\mu)$ whose residual is orthogonal to every $p_i$, $0\le i\le N$.
source_evidence.case_anchor: If $v\in V_N(\mu)$ has the same residual property, then $w=v-\Pi_Nu$ lies in $V_N(\mu)$ and is orthogonal to every basis vector, hence to itself. Positive definiteness in [F2] gives $\int w^2\,d\mu=0$, so $w=0$ in $L^2(\mu)$ and $v=\Pi_Nu$. This proves uniqueness. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: Each numerator is finite by [F3], and each denominator $h_j$ is finite and strictly positive by [F1]–[F2]. Thus every coefficient in the displayed finite sum is a defined real number. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]
actualproofparagraphs.2.1: Orthogonality of the $p_j$ gives, for each $i\le N$, $\int (u-\Pi_Nu)p_i\,d\mu =\int u p_i\,d\mu-\sum_{j=0}^{N}\frac{\int u p_j\,d\mu}{h_j}\int p_jp_i\,d\mu =0,$ because all terms with $j\ne i$ vanish and the $j=i$ term equals $\int u p_i\,d\mu$. Thus $\Pi_Nu\in V_N(\mu)$ has the required residual orthogonality. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]
